articles.title: iFixit’s Apple HomeView teardown reveals a device that will be difficult to repair
articles.text:
After finding recent versions of Apple’s iPads and HomePods much easier to disassemble for battery replacements or other repairs, iFixit assumed it would be the same story for Apple’s new HomeView hub that looks like a seven-inch tablet stuck to a smart speaker. The reality was much different and by the time they got the HomeView apart iFixit’s skilled techs had “ripped a connector, snapped a speaker in two, and put more force on the poor logic board than any of us were comfortable with.”
iFixit’s Apple HomeView teardown reveals a device that will be difficult to repair
Apple’s inroads on designing repairable devices seems to have been abandoned with the HomeView.
The tablet section of the HomeView proved to be the bigger challenge to disassemble as a result of some questionable decisions with Apple’s design. The glue used to secure the display in place “held on harder than on any Apple product we’ve opened recently,” iFixit says. And while Apple’s decision to turn the HomeView’s entire aluminum chassis into a heat sink was clever, the thermal bond between a heat shield and the device’s logic board made separating the two a “remarkably risky operation.” While these design decisions possibly streamlined assembly at a factory, the extensive use of glue makes servicing the HomeView incredibly difficult.
In an accompanying teardown video iFixit also reveals how much smaller the speaker drivers are in the wall-mounted version of the HomeView versus the tabletop option. Although both versions are priced at $299, the wall version costs a little more when you factor in the required mount that’s not included, leaving iFixit feeling that you’re getting less performance while spending more money.

articles.title: Think Twice Before Using Your Laptop On Any Soft Surface - Engadget
articles.text:
Think twice before using your laptop on any soft surface
Sat down cozy with your laptop? Well, just make sure you're not too cozy — as you could be causing some serious damage.
The portability of laptops is their chief selling point over powerful, immobile PC rigs. These machines are great for getting work done on the go or while sitting comfortably. However, there are pitfalls that can come from getting a little too comfortable with where you take your laptop.
If you've ever found your laptop fans getting loud without good reason, especially when you're not up to anything that would give your CPU a workout, you might be overheating your machine without knowing it. While the source might lie in unnecessary programs chugging along or components that have passed their prime, the problem could also be external. In fact, if the surface you keep your laptop on is soft and plush, it could be blocking your device's airflow and damaging its battery.
How soft surfaces cause laptop overheating
Many laptops have their ventilation slots on the bottom of the device — a consequence of their compact design. This isn't typically a problem, as most have rubber feet underneath to slightly elevate them on a smooth surface, allowing for a small gap that can facilitate good airflow.
Unfortunately, soft surfaces like bed covers, cushions or pillows bunch up, and thin metal laptops tend to sink into these plush materials. This presses the surface right up to the bottom of the chassis, blocking the fans and causing the temperature of the laptop's CPU to rise.
Soft surfaces also act as insulators, trapping heat and accelerating the warming process. Because laptops sink into these surfaces, they press the fabric's dust and debris into the fans. That dust buildup can also degrade your laptop's airflow.
All of this trapped heat builds up within your laptop, causing its fan to accelerate and placing more strain on the battery. Not only does all this heat strain lithium-ion batteries, but it could also lead to permanent battery damage.
Battery damage from soft surfaces and what to do about it
It's plain to see how using a laptop on a soft surface could lead to reduced performance, damage or even total battery death after a long enough period. If you want to get ahead of this issue, the obvious first step is to avoid soft surfaces and place your laptop down on a table instead of your lap, bed or sofa.
If you still prefer the convenience of comfier setups, invest in a cooling pad, which will provide better airflow underneath your machine. If you suspect that your vents are clogged with dust, you can clean your laptop fan. Just turn off your laptop and blast the vents with electronics-safe compressed air for a simple clean.

articles.title: Google to keep Gemini chats for 2 months, up from 72 hours, even with history off | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google is extending how long it keeps temporary Gemini chats and conversations made with chat history turned off to around two months, saying the change aims to improve safety and security as AI systems become more capable.
The change, which will roll out globally in the Gemini app over the coming weeks, marks a significant increase from the previous 72-hour retention period mentioned in Google’s Gemini Apps Privacy Hub, according to an archived version from November 12.
OpenAI, by comparison, says it may keep temporary chats in ChatGPT for up to 30 days, whereas Anthropic retains incognito chats in Claude for 30 days by default. However, companies may keep some data longer for legal or safety reasons, or to investigate policy violations.
Google did not answer questions about what prompted the change and whether it would affect how conversations are accessed or reviewed, instead pointing to a blog post that says chats are kept longer to respond to users, process feedback, and protect its services and users. Its updated Gemini Apps Privacy Hub also cites potential system failures as a reason for retaining chats and says temporary conversations are not used to train AI models.
The longer retention period comes as Google introduces separate settings for Gemini’s chat history and AI training. Until now, both were tied to a single “Keep Activity” setting. Users will now be able to keep their conversations in their chat history without using them to train Google’s generative AI models.
Google says both new settings will be turned off by default for users who previously disabled Keep Activity. For those who had Keep Activity turned on, their chat history will remain enabled. They can, though, decide separately whether Google can use their conversations to train AI models.

articles.title: Nvidia says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.text:
Starting Nvidia’s quarterly earnings call on Tuesday, new board chair Harvey Jones said that when former CEO Jensen Huang resigned, “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.”
Nvidia says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
The board said it would not take additional questions on the call about Huang’s departure.
Jones added, “We will not be addressing or taking questions on today’s call regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation.”
Huang had publicly floated the idea of returning earlier on Tuesday. In a statement posted to X, he wrote that he “did not live up to the standards expected of everyone” at the company, that he regretted his mistakes, and that he would cooperate with the Nvidia board’s investigation into his actions. He added that he’d be willing to return to the chief executive role if offered it, though a day earlier, the Nvidia board reportedly said it was not considering bringing him back. “NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company,” Huang wrote. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”
But since his November 12th resignation, Huang remains entangled in scandal. He’s reportedly had three affairs, two with subordinates at Nvidia, one with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset suspected of facilitating illicit chip sales. (Huang has pushed against restrictions on Nvidia chip sales in China.) He’s scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1st, and an internal company investigation is ongoing.
Tech industry heavyweights have still voiced their support for Huang, dubbing him “irreplaceable” and petitioning for his return. Some have cast doubt on the allegations that Alice Huang (no relation) was spying on behalf of China and painted the leaks about their relationship as a conspiracy against the former CEO. President Donald Trump, a close ally of Huang for much of the past year, has also backed him. On Monday, Trump said he “would not mind” Huang returning, adding that “I think he learned a big lesson — I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another.”
Trump’s closeness with Huang could also complicate things for Nvidia, however. The company has ramped up its lobbying in Washington, D.C., spending $5 million in 2025 and $4.7 million so far in 2026. But as Democrats prepare to take Congress, they’re planning to investigate Trump’s dealings with Big Tech and other industries, alleging potential corruption. “The election wasn’t very positive for AI, and [the news around Huang’s resignation] is only going to complicate things, especially for the company in particular but for AI as a whole going forward,” Brendan Glavin, director of insights at OpenSecrets, told The Verge in an interview last week.
Lior Prosor, managing partner at Deep33, a tech VC firm, said last week that he didn’t expect Huang’s resignation to pop the AI bubble, although Huang has had a significant hand in mobilizing funds for the AI infrastructure buildout in the U.S. Under Huang’s leadership in August, Nvidia entered into partnerships with six financial institutions for about $500 billion to fund such endeavors. “NVIDIA supplies roughly 75 percent of the AI compute hardware the industry consumes, and demand continues to dramatically outpace supply,” Deep33’s Prosor said in an interview with The Verge. “Neither its customers nor its competitors can easily replace the capabilities it provides, and the economic incentives driving the AI trade remain unchanged.”
Even so, a potential market cooling has some worried, as Anthropic’s IPO, slated to potentially be the largest of all time, is set for Thursday. The chipmaker had agreed to buy $10 billion in Anthropic shares via private placement, on top of a $10 billion funding promise Nvidia had already made last year.

articles.title: As decision model use skyrockets, is customization the next frontier? | TechCrunch
articles.text:
In October, more than one in four requests on Vercel’s AI model router went to decision models, not LLMs — an enormous share of work for a kind of computerized intelligence that was invented only a month earlier.
Decision models are LLMs that don’t produce output tokens; instead, they’re tuned to use their general intelligence to quickly and cheaply decide between preset options, while registering its level of confidence in the choice. They’re useful in production environments, where fast decisions can be more important than the reasoning provided by a slower and more expensive frontier model.
TypeSafe became a $7.5 billion company after releasing its Jev family of models, which continues to dominate usage (at least where we can see metrics from services like OpenRouter, which handled more than 1.5 billion queries to TypeSafe’s models last week).
However, it’s easy to make a decision model, and dozens were released in the wake of Jev. One Amazon engineer made one in a weekend, and soon every hyperscaler had its own option. On Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said that his company is rolling out its decision model, Microsoft-Decision-1.1, for wide use on Azure immediately.
The action is happening on both ends of the ecosystem: Sqwish, a U.K.-based AI startup behind a decision model called kettei fat, announced a $3 million pre-seed round today. Co-founders Ushnish Sengupta and Federica Freddi, who met as Cambridge grad students, had been developing small LLMs when Jev arrived on the scene, and they realized their architectures could be repurposed as a powerful decision model.
Data appears to be the key to a successful model in this category — TypeSafe CEO Diogo Almeida told TechCrunch that the hardest part of building Jev was finely calibrating its judgement using statistically-adjusted synthetic data. Sqwish, too, has been working with synthetic data, but its unique offering is built-in post-training tools that use a customer’s own data to improve the model’s judgement.
“What makes us not a commodity, I think, is the fact that we are offering our customers the same power…they can keep uploading their production data, and just the same way that we trained our models, their models can also keep getting better at the tasks that they care about,” CEO Ushnish Sengupta told TechCrunch.
Attempting to rank decision models is difficult; Sqwish’s “kettei fat” model has performed well on some benchmarks, but most builders of the technology say that the real proof is in the pudding: It’s generally simple for developers to sub in one model for another and see how it does in a specific context.
“The benchmark is more of an invitation to try the model out, and then the continual tuning is the reason why they should stick to us,” Sengupta said.
The Microsoft-Decision-1.1 model is also the result of the company carefully balancing across cost, latency, intelligence and calibration. Achint Srivastava, the engineering VP who led the project, agreed that too much focus on benchmarks is a mistake.
“What we see is that ‘benchmaxed’ models fall flat under real enterprise usage very quickly,” Srivastava wrote in an email. “Our testing underscores just how challenging it is to deliver accuracy, reliability, speed and cost efficiency in a single model. Microsoft-Decision-1.1 and Jev are among the few that perform strongly across all four dimensions, even when evaluated on ‘held out’ or unseen benchmarks reflective of real use cases.”
For startups like Sqwish, competition with hyperscalers and frontier labs is an opportunity. Freddi predicts that future systems will see so-called System One intelligence, like decision models, working in concert with System Two intelligence, like frontier LLMs.
“Even in that future, System One is maybe a $10 billion, $50 billion [opportunity], and OpenAI is doing this IPO with you know $1 trillion, $2 trillion market value in mind,” she told TechCrunch. “This is all we care about; whereas for them, this is just a side project.”

articles.title: Từ kẻ thách thức đến ngôi vương tại Việt Nam: Tham vọng của Xiaomi không dừng ở thị phần smartphone
articles.text:
Chip, hệ điều hành và mô hình AI tự phát triển lần đầu cùng có mặt trên một chiếc flagship, hệ sinh thái Human × Car × Home mở rộng từ điện thoại sang xe điện và gia dụng cỡ lớn, và mặt lưng điện thoại trở thành một màn hình. Ông Niu Chen, Tổng Giám đốc Xiaomi Việt Nam, chia sẻ về năm 2026 của Xiaomi và điều người dùng Việt có thể chờ ở thế hệ Xiaomi 18 Pro Series.
Khởi đầu là một công ty phát triển phần mềm cho điện thoại, Xiaomi đã mất hơn 15 năm để đưa hệ sinh thái thiết bị của mình vượt ra khỏi phạm vi smartphone. Đến nay, đây là hãng duy nhất xây dựng được nền tảng ba trụ cột “Human x Car x Home”, gồm thiết bị cá nhân, xe điện và nhà thông minh.
Và ngay trong năm nay, hãng đã giới thiệu chiếc smartphone đầu tiên hội tụ ba công nghệ do hãng tự phát triển là chip, hệ điều hành HyperOS 4 và mô hình AI.
Với người dùng Việt Nam, dấu mốc gần nhất là Xiaomi 18 Pro Series, thế hệ flagship lần đầu ra mắt toàn cầu và đến Việt Nam cùng thời điểm, với màn hình phía sau và camera Leica. Chúng tôi đã có cuộc trò chuyện với ông Niu Chen, Tổng giám đốc Xiaomi Việt Nam về những chuyển động này.
Phần I. Hệ sinh thái Human × Car × Home và tự chủ công nghệ
Nếu phải chọn một thay đổi công nghệ quan trọng nhất của Xiaomi trong năm 2026, Ông sẽ chọn điều gì: AI, chip tự phát triển hay hệ sinh thái Human × Car × Home?
Năm 2026 đánh dấu bước tiến quan trọng của Xiaomi khi lần đầu tiên tích hợp chip, hệ điều hành và mô hình AI lớn do chúng tôi tự phát triển trên một thiết bị flagship đầu bảng. Đây là bước chuyển từ những đột phá công nghệ riêng lẻ sang năng lực phối hợp đồng bộ ở cấp độ hệ thống.
Chiến lược “Human × Car × Home” là định hướng dài hạn của Xiaomi, trong đó AI giữ vai trò then chốt để nâng tầm trải nghiệm, còn chip và hệ điều hành tự phát triển tạo nên nền tảng công nghệ. Sự kết hợp này cho phép chúng tôi lấy nhu cầu người dùng làm trọng tâm, tối ưu trải nghiệm xuyên suốt từ phần cứng, hệ điều hành đến các dịch vụ thông minh. Một cột mốc thể hiện định hướng đó là mẫu điện thoại màn hình gập Xiaomi 18 Fold, được giới thiệu vào tháng 9 năm nay. Đây là thiết bị đầu tiên tích hợp đồng thời ba công nghệ do Xiaomi tự phát triển: chip XRING O3, hệ điều hành Xiaomi HyperOS 4 và mô hình AI lớn MiMo chạy trực tiếp trên thiết bị, qua đó đưa năng lực tự chủ công nghệ của Xiaomi vào một trải nghiệm sản phẩm thống nhất.
Trong ba công nghệ này, chip XRING O3 đã được sản xuất hàng loạt và đưa vào ứng dụng thương mại. Đây là một trong ba dòng chip Xiaomi đang phát triển; hai dòng còn lại tập trung vào tăng tốc AI và hỗ trợ lái xe thông minh, dự kiến được thương mại hóa vào năm tới. Như vậy, Xiaomi đang đồng thời thúc đẩy ba hướng nghiên cứu và phát triển chip: SoC cho điện thoại, chip tăng tốc AI và chip phục vụ lái xe thông minh. Song song với phần cứng, Xiaomi cũng đang hoàn thiện nền tảng AI và phần mềm. MiMo hiện có hệ thống mô hình bao gồm ngôn ngữ, đa phương thức và giọng nói, trong khi Xiaomi HyperOS 4 đã hoàn tất tái cấu trúc nền tảng cốt lõi. Trên cơ sở đó, trợ lý AI được nâng cấp với năng lực của mô hình AI lớn, cho phép phối hợp giữa điện thoại, máy tính bảng, ô tô và các thiết bị gia dụng thông minh. Xiaomi cũng đã xây dựng ba nhà máy thông minh trong các lĩnh vực điện thoại, ô tô và điện gia dụng, tạo nền tảng sản xuất để đưa công nghệ tự phát triển vào các sản phẩm phục vụ người tiêu dùng.
Định hướng tự chủ công nghệ này được xây dựng trên nền tảng đầu tư dài hạn. Trong gần 5 năm qua, chúng tôi đã đầu tư tổng cộng 105,5 tỷ nhân dân tệ (15,8 tỷ USD) vào các lĩnh vực công nghệ cốt lõi. Riêng với lĩnh vực chip, Xiaomi đặt kế hoạch đầu tư 50 tỷ nhân dân tệ (7,5 tỷ USD) trong 10 năm và đến nay đã giải ngân 21 tỷ nhân dân tệ (khoảng 3,2 tỷ USD). Trước đó, các thiết bị sử dụng chip XRING O1 đã đạt hơn một triệu chiếc xuất xưởng, tạo tiền đề để Xiaomi tiếp tục mở rộng ứng dụng công nghệ tự phát triển trên quy mô thương mại.
Tại IFA 2026, Xiaomi nói về việc đưa AI “beyond the screen”. Smartphone AI hiện tại đã có rất nhiều tính năng. Vì sao vẫn cần đi xa hơn?
Điện thoại AI đã giúp người dùng cảm nhận rõ sự tiện lợi của công nghệ thông minh, đồng thời là một cửa ngõ quan trọng để tiếp cận hệ sinh thái “Human × Car × Home” của Xiaomi. Khi đưa AI “bước ra khỏi màn hình” (beyond the screen), chúng tôi muốn mở rộng sự tiện lợi ấy sang những bối cảnh thực tế như sinh hoạt trong gia đình hay di chuyển, giúp người dùng hoàn thành những tác vụ phức tạp hơn.
Nhu cầu của người dùng thường liên quan đến nhiều thiết bị và nhiều bước thực hiện. Chẳng hạn, khi người dùng sắp về đến nhà, các thiết bị gia dụng có thể chủ động điều chỉnh không gian sống; hay chỉ với một câu lệnh, ảnh trong điện thoại được gửi đến máy in để in ra. Điều này đòi hỏi AI phải hiểu ý định của người dùng, nhận biết bối cảnh và điều phối các thiết bị cùng thực hiện.
Vì vậy, chúng tôi liên tục thúc đẩy sự phối hợp giữa chipset, hệ điều hành, mô hình AI lớn và các thiết bị, để AI tiến từ việc cung cấp câu trả lời đến thực sự hoàn thành tác vụ. Thước đo cho bước tiến này là khả năng giúp người dùng giảm thao tác, tiết kiệm thời gian và có cuộc sống nhẹ nhàng hơn một cách ổn định, đáng tin cậy. Ngành AI đang bước vào một giai đoạn phát triển mới: các mô hình lớn giúp máy móc biết “tư duy”, còn AI vật lý cần tiến xa hơn, giúp máy móc hiểu thế giới thực và phục vụ con người trong đời sống hằng ngày.
Có thể nói Xiaomi không còn muốn được nhìn nhận đơn thuần là một hãng smartphone?
Smartphone là thế mạnh vốn có. Xiaomi hiện giữ vững vị trí Top 3 trên toàn cầu, và Top 1 thị phần tại Việt Nam (theo báo cáo thị phần phân phối smartphone của Omdia Quý III/2026).
| Việt Nam: Top các nhà sản xuất smartphone, Quý 3/2026 |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Thứ hạng | Hãng sản xuất | Thị phần sản lượng | Tăng trưởng hàng năm | 
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Xiaomi | 27% | ▲ 50% | 
| 2 | Samsung | 27% | ▼ -3% | 
| 3 | Apple | 19% | ▲ 15% | 
| 4 | OPPO | 16% | ▼ -31% | 
| 5 | vivo | 7% | ▲ 7% | 
Smartphone vẫn là trụ cột chính, tuy nhiên động lực tăng trưởng dài hạn nằm ở toàn bộ hệ sinh thái Human × Car × Home.
Xiaomi là thương hiệu duy nhất trên toàn cầu sở hữu hệ sinh thái Human x Car x Home. Hệ sinh thái kết nối giúp chúng tôi gia tăng trải nghiệm cho người dùng và mở rộng kinh doanh. Tiêu biểu là chúng tôi đang chuẩn bị ra mắt xe điện trên thị trường quốc tế từ năm 2027.
Smart Home đã tồn tại hơn một thập kỷ, nhưng nhiều sản phẩm hiện nay vẫn chỉ là thiết bị thông thường có thêm Wi-Fi. Chúng tôi muốn sản phẩm của mình có thể thiết lập nâng cao để mang đến nhiều tiện nghi hơn. Màn “trình diễn” với hơn 380 sản phẩm trong không gian 3.300 m² tại IFA vừa qua của Xiaomi không chỉ thể hiện quy mô, mà lợi thế cạnh tranh còn nằm ở khả năng phối hợp giữa các thiết bị.
Hiện nay, dòng sản phẩm gia dụng Mijia của chúng tôi có hơn 2.000 sản phẩm thuộc hơn 130 ngành hàng, được kết nối trong cùng một hệ sinh thái. Dựa trên năng lực về AI, hệ điều hành và kết nối IoT, Mijia tích hợp công nghệ thông minh vào các thiết bị gia dụng truyền thống, mang đến cuộc sống hằng ngày thông minh, trực quan và liền mạch hơn.
Nhờ hệ sinh thái đa dạng như vậy, đến nay chúng tôi hiện đã có hơn 776 triệu người dùng và kết nối hơn 1,16 tỷ thiết bị trên toàn cầu.
Khi Human × Home đang được đẩy mạnh trên toàn cầu, bao giờ Xiaomi sẽ mở rộng trụ cột “Car” ra quốc tế? Việt Nam có nằm trong kế hoạch này không?
Dù mới gia nhập ngành ô tô, Xiaomi đã đạt được những kết quả rất tích cực.
Từ đợt bàn giao Xiaomi SU7 đầu tiên vào tháng 4/2024 đến ngày 07/09/2026, Xiaomi đã bàn giao hơn 800.000 xe. Từ Xiaomi SU7, Xiaomi SU7 Ultra, Xiaomi YU7 đến dòng Xiaomi SkyNomad hoàn toàn mới, các sản phẩm của chúng tôi tiếp tục nhận được sự đánh giá cao và thu hút sự quan tâm của cộng đồng yêu ô tô trên toàn thế giới.
Chúng tôi có kế hoạch gia nhập thị trường châu Âu từ năm 2027, bắt đầu với Đức. Việc mở rộng ra thị trường quốc tế đòi hỏi một hệ thống phân phối, dịch vụ và hậu mãi vững chắc, bảo đảm trải nghiệm sở hữu và sử dụng xe lâu dài cho khách hàng.
Hiện chúng tôi chưa xác nhận thời điểm ra mắt ô tô Xiaomi tại Việt Nam. Chúng tôi vẫn đang phát triển ổn định hoạt động kinh doanh thiết bị di động và gia dụng thông minh tại đây, đồng thời tiếp tục mang đến những sản phẩm, dịch vụ chất lượng cao để xây dựng niềm tin và sự gắn bó lâu dài với ngày càng nhiều người tiêu dùng.
Phần II. Gia dụng cỡ lớn
Danh mục sản phẩm của Xiaomi có đồ gia dụng cỡ lớn từ lâu. Lý do nào hãng cho rằng đây là thời điểm tốt để kinh doanh gia dụng lớn ở Việt Nam?
Xiaomi đánh giá cao tiềm năng của ngành gia dụng thông minh tại Việt Nam. Việt Nam có hơn 102 triệu dân, hàng triệu người dùng yêu thích công nghệ và có dư địa lớn cho nhu cầu nâng cấp gia dụng theo hướng tiết kiệm, tiện lợi và kết nối thông minh.
Chúng tôi mong muốn đưa những thế mạnh Xiaomi đã tích lũy trong công nghệ thông minh, thiết kế sản phẩm và kết nối hệ sinh thái vào nhiều khía cạnh hơn trong đời sống hằng ngày của người dùng Việt Nam. Các thiết bị gia dụng lớn gắn liền với sinh hoạt gia đình, đồng thời mở ra nhiều ứng dụng thiết thực hơn cho việc kết nối điện thoại, thiết bị thông minh và không gian sống. Qua đó, chúng tôi hướng đến việc giúp người dùng Việt Nam tận hưởng cuộc sống tiện nghi hơn nhờ công nghệ.
Sau gần 10 năm phát triển ở mảng smartphone và AIoT tại Việt Nam, gia dụng thông minh sẽ là bước mở rộng chiến lược để từng bước hiện thực hóa hệ sinh thái Human × Car × Home.
So với di động, tôi nghĩ đặc điểm cơ bản của TV, tủ lạnh, điều hòa là vòng đời dài hơn. Để bán loại hàng này, Xiaomi có cần thay đổi gì từ nội tại để sẵn sàng cho một cuộc chơi rất khác chưa?
Trước hết, Xiaomi đã sẵn sàng với năng lực sản xuất mạnh mẽ ở quy mô toàn cầu. Chúng tôi đã hoàn thiện 3 nhà máy chủ chốt: điện thoại thông minh, ô tô và thiết bị gia dụng. Trong đó, mới nhất và nổi bật nhất là nhà máy thiết bị gia dụng tại Vũ Hán vận hành từ tháng 10/2025 với diện tích 500.000 m² và tổng vốn đầu tư 2,5 tỷ NDT. Ở tốc độ sản xuất cao nhất, cứ mỗi 6,5 giây lại có một chiếc điều hòa xuất xưởng.
Xiaomi đặt chất lượng sản phẩm lên hàng đầu và kiểm soát chất lượng từ quá trình sản xuất. Nhà máy hiện đại được tích hợp nghiên cứu và phát triển, sản xuất và kiểm định chất lượng, và được trang bị đến 46 phòng thí nghiệm.
Danh mục sản phẩm gia dụng cũng ngày càng đa dạng. Chúng tôi liên tục mở rộng danh mục Mijia với tủ lạnh, máy giặt, điều hòa và đáp ứng đa dạng nhu cầu và phân khúc khác nhau. Mới nhất là chiếc máy giặt sấy flagship máy giặt sấy 3 lồng Mijia Tri-Drum Washer Dryer Pro 14.5Kg và tủ lạnh cao cấp Mijia Cross-Door Refrigerator Pro 560L cũng sẽ ra mắt tại Việt Nam. Cho thấy tầm quan trọng của thị trường Việt Nam trong chiến lược phát triển mảng gia dụng của chúng tôi.
Ngoài ra, dịch vụ hậu mãi chất lượng cũng là yếu tố then chốt. Việc mở rộng sang lĩnh vực gia dụng phải đi cùng năng lực phân phối, lắp đặt, bảo hành và chăm sóc khách hàng.
Kể từ khi gia nhập thị trường Việt Nam từ năm 2017, bên cạnh các mục tiêu tăng trưởng kinh doanh, chúng tôi đã không ngừng nâng cao năng lực phân phối, vận hành và hậu mãi, hướng đến sự phát triển ổn định trong dài hạn. Tại Việt Nam, Xiaomi đã xây dựng mạng lưới 66 điểm bảo hành và dịch vụ trên toàn quốc dành cho thiết bị AIoT, đồng thời khai trương trung tâm bảo hành chuyên dụng đầu tiên cho thiết bị gia dụng lớn tại TPHCM.
Các thiết bị thương hiệu Mijia Series được áp dụng chính sách bảo hành dài hơn mức thông thường. Máy lạnh, tủ lạnh và máy giặt được bảo hành 24 tháng; máy nén máy lạnh và tủ lạnh được bảo hành 10 năm, mô-tơ máy giặt cửa trên 3 năm và mô-tơ máy giặt sấy cửa trước đến 12 năm, gần như trọn vòng đời sản phẩm. Đây là tiêu chuẩn bảo hành cao nhất và thể hiện sự cam kết của Xiaomi dù vừa mới “tấn công” vào mảng kinh doanh này gần đây.
Phần III. Xiaomi 18 Pro Max và chuẩn flagship mới của Xiaomi
Xiaomi 18 Pro Max thu hút sự chú ý của truyền thông. Nếu bỏ bảng thông số sang một bên, Xiaomi 18 Pro Series cho thấy điều gì về hướng phát triển tiếp theo của flagship Xiaomi?
Nếu chỉ nhìn Xiaomi 18 Pro Series qua chipset, độ phân giải megapixel trên camera hay dung lượng pin, chúng ta sẽ bỏ lỡ điều thú vị nhất: ngày càng nhiều trải nghiệm được tạo ra bằng cách kết hợp thiết kế phần cứng, phần mềm và AI cùng lúc.
Khi cấu hình và thiết kế smartphone ngày càng tương đồng, dư địa tăng trưởng của flagship nằm ở trải nghiệm mới đủ giá trị để thuyết phục người dùng nâng cấp.
Màn hình phía sau là một ví dụ: mở ra cách xem thông tin nhanh hơn, chụp ảnh thuận tiện hơn và cá nhân hóa bằng AI và thể hiện phong cách cá nhân nhiều hơn. Giá trị của thiết kế mới nằm ở những tiện ích người dùng thực sự cảm nhận mỗi ngày.
Đó là cách Xiaomi xây dựng vị thế cao cấp: tạo khác biệt mà người dùng thấy hữu ích và sẵn sàng lựa chọn.
“Giá trị của thiết kế mới nằm ở những tiện ích người dùng thực sự cảm nhận mỗi ngày.”
Màn hình phụ từng xuất hiện và từng bị xem là gimmick (chiêu trò). Xiaomi có lo điều đó lặp lại?
Có một sự thật rằng: Trong những năm gần đây, hiệu năng, camera và AI trên smartphone đã có nhiều bước tiến, nhưng thiết kế và cách thức sử dụng lại ngày càng tương đồng. Theo tôi, cơ hội đổi mới tiếp theo nằm ở việc mở ra những cách tương tác hữu ích hơn, giúp người dùng cảm nhận rõ giá trị của công nghệ trong đời sống hằng ngày.
Khi màn hình phía trước đã đạt mức độ hoàn thiện cao, chúng tôi nhìn thấy tiềm năng ở mặt lưng điện thoại như một không gian tương tác mới. Màn hình phụ phía sau cho phép người dùng nắm bắt nhanh thông tin khi đặt úp máy, chụp selfie bằng hệ thống camera sau Leica, sử dụng các công cụ sáng tạo và cá nhân hóa trải nghiệm bằng AI. Đây cũng là không gian để thể hiện dấu ấn riêng qua hình ảnh, hình nền hay những ứng dụng nhỏ phù hợp với nhu cầu của mỗi người.
Để những ý tưởng đó trở thành trải nghiệm thiết thực, Xiaomi cần tối ưu đồng bộ phần cứng và phần mềm, từ chất lượng hiển thị, camera đến thao tác điều khiển và hiệu quả năng lượng. Với chúng tôi, giá trị của đổi mới được thể hiện qua những điều rất cụ thể: người dùng tiếp cận thông tin nhanh hơn, thao tác đơn giản hơn và có thêm cách sáng tạo, thể hiện phong cách cá nhân dễ dàng hơn trên thiết bị luôn đồng hành cùng mình.
Chúng tôi luôn lắng nghe phản hồi và tiếp tục hoàn thiện trải nghiệm. Nhưng cuối cùng, người dùng mới là người quyết định một công nghệ trở thành tương lai hay không.
“Nhưng cuối cùng, người dùng mới là người quyết định một công nghệ trở thành tương lai hay không.”
Xiaomi 18 Pro Series đã được xác nhận sẽ đến Việt Nam. Người dùng Việt có thể kỳ vọng điều gì?
Nếu chỉ được hé lộ về Xiaomi 18 Pro Series tại Việt Nam bằng một câu, tôi sẽ nói: đừng chỉ chờ một chiếc flagship cấu hình mạnh hơn.
Nếu nhìn vào Xiaomi 18 Pro Series tại Trung Quốc, người dùng Việt có thể kỳ vọng một thế hệ flagship kết hợp sâu hơn giữa phần cứng, phần mềm và AI.
Xiaomi 18 Pro Series tại Việt Nam sẽ không đơn thuần là một bản nâng cấp cấu hình. Người dùng có thể tận hưởng nhiều trải nghiệm flagship như khả năng nhiếp ảnh Leica với bộ đôi camera chính và tele 200MP để ghi lại chi tiết từ gần đến xa, selfie bằng camera sau với khả năng xem trước khung hình trên màn hình phụ, thể hiện cá tính qua hình nền AI và mini app tùy biến theo nhu cầu, cùng chipset mạnh mẽ giúp xử lý mượt mà từ đa nhiệm đến chơi game và AI hỗ trợ sáng tạo, cá nhân hóa trải nghiệm hằng ngày...
Và phải nhấn mạnh, đây là lần đầu tiên Xiaomi 18 Pro Series ra mắt trên toàn cầu. Người dùng Việt Nam sẽ được trải nghiệm cùng thời điểm với toàn cầu, khẳng định tầm quan trọng của thị trường Việt Nam trong chiến lược của Xiaomi.
“Đừng chỉ chờ một chiếc flagship cấu hình mạnh hơn.”

articles.title: Ambience's AI now helps hospitals plan rounds and discharges
articles.text:
Ambience Healthcare has added Rounding Assistant and Discharge Readiness to its hospital AI software, to help care teams prioritise tasks and spot barriers to discharge earlier. The company also points to customer results on billing, including a 6.5% rise in case mix index at Onvida Health.
Ambience Healthcare has added two AI tools that help hospital teams decide what to do next for each patient, the company announced on Tuesday. They join its existing software, which writes clinical notes and suggests billing codes for hospital stays.
Rounding Assistant pulls together overnight events, changes in a patient’s condition and a list of suggested tasks for each shift. Discharge Readiness flags medical, practical and social problems that could delay a patient going home, earlier in the stay.
Ambience is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins and the OpenAI Startup Fund. It counts Cleveland Clinic and Mayo Clinic among its customers, and ties its fees to results. Cleveland Clinic has also backed Dyania, another hospital AI startup.
Much of the pitch is about money. Ambience aims to raise hospitals’ case mix index, a measure of how sick patients are that helps set what insurers pay. At Onvida Health, discharges handled with Ambience scored 6.5% higher than a year earlier, the company says.
“To justify the investment, we needed roughly a 1.5% improvement in case mix index,” said Mike Lewis, chief financial officer of Onvida Medical Group.
Lewis said Onvida’s own finance team checked the results. Ambience also says admission notes written with its tool captured 59% more of the diagnoses used in quality rankings, in one health system’s review of 1,100 stays. None of the figures come from independent research.
AI note tools are still under scrutiny. In August, England’s patient watchdog warned that AI scribes were getting drug names and diagnoses wrong. Rivals are growing fast too: Heidi raised $340M in September, and Google launched Gemini for healthcare last week.

articles.title: Snapchat Has Finally Made It Easy To Check An Account's Mutual Friends - Engadget
articles.text:
Snapchat has finally made it easy to check an account's mutual friends
The new feature is available in the US, Australia, France and Sweden.
Snapchat has finally added a Mutual Friends feature, 15 years after the platform launched. As expected, this makes it easy to check accounts for any friends in common. The tool should provide crucial information that informs whether or not a friend request is accepted.
If an account comes through as a request and it's a ghost town with nary a friend in common, it likely indicates a refusal. The same goes if there are too many friends in common and you really just aren't up for sharing. This should help find that Snapchat sweet spot.
It works exactly how you think it does. The mutual friends are displayed directly on the other user's profile. That's pretty much it. This is, however, a fully opt-in experience. That means that both accounts have to turn the feature on in order for it to work. This looks easy enough to do, as it happens via a new prompt. It's turned off by default, as Snapchatters do tend to enjoy discretion.
The Mutual Friends feature is available right now for users in the US, France, Sweden and Australia on both iOS and Android. We don't know when it's coming to the rest of the world, though Engadget has reached out to Snapchat for some clarification. We'll update this post when we find out more.
$SNAP I was recently pitching snap on a buyout of Partiful an event planning site/app but looks like they built their own version in-app, even better @evanspiegel
Introducing Snapchat Plans, a new suite of features that gives Snapchatters a new way to create, share, and manage... pic.twitter.com/KXXFUfbhLv
— Lukas Kafka (@Kafka7invest) September 10, 2026
This is just the latest feature the company has added to its social media platform. There's a new event planning tool and a paid storage option. This has been a good year for the company. It recently boasted of more than 30 million paid subscribers on Snapchat+ and related plans.

articles.title: Google buys Howie, an AI assistant that books your meetings
articles.text:
Google Labs has bought Howie, an AI scheduling tool that users copy into emails to arrange meetings, Bloomberg reported. Terms were not disclosed; PitchBook valued Howie at $14M in 2024. Google said it wants to build AI tools for small businesses with the team.
Google has bought Howie, an AI tool that schedules meetings and manages calendars, Bloomberg reported. Google Labs, the company’s experimental arm, announced the deal on Monday in a post on X. It did not share the price.
Howie works like a human assistant. Users copy it into an email thread, and it finds a time and books the meeting. PitchBook valued the startup at $14M in 2024, according to Bloomberg.
Google Labs said it wants to build “the next generation of intuitive AI tools” for small businesses with the Howie team.
Howie’s co-founder and CEO, Austin Petersmith, said the team will keep building the tool at Google. He noted on LinkedIn that Howie has always run on Gmail and Google Calendar. Google has not said whether Howie will be built into its own apps.
The deal adds to Google’s push into AI agents that act for users, not just answer questions. In May, it launched Gemini Spark, an always-on agent that takes tasks by email. In October, it gave workplace agents their own email addresses.
OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and xAI all offer rival agents, and OpenAI bought travel agent Odessia last week.
Google Labs has been busy. Last week it released Tabletop, a tool for building group planning apps with AI. In February, it bought music app ProducerAI, which runs on Google DeepMind’s Lyria model.

articles.title: How To Sideload Apps On iOS (Even If You're In The US) - Engadget
articles.text:
How to sideload apps on iOS (even if you're in the US)
Alternative App Marketplaces are only available in a few regions, but you can sideload iOS apps anywhere with right tools.
Apple's App Store was for years the only place where you could download official iOS apps. However, recent regulatory changes in places like the European Union and Japan have helped to push Apple to not only detail how third-party app stores and payments will work but also to allow alternative app marketplaces on iOS. For example, Apple opened up third-party app stores in Brazil only after a judge ordered the company to allow sideloading in the region. Even if you're in the US, there's still a way to take advantage of sideloading. Apple allows anyone with a free Apple Developer account to sign and install apps from outside the App Store for development purposes. Taking things further, tools like AltStore Classic and Sideloadly have turned this into a way to install compatible IPA files — the file format for iOS apps.
It's not as easy as in countries where alternative app marketplaces are available, and there are also some drawbacks. Apps signed with a free account expire after seven days and must be re-signed, and you can only sideload three apps at a time. Still, it's an option in the US if you really want to try out a specific app that you can't find on the App Store.
How to sideload apps on iOS using a PC or Mac
There are two different versions of AltStore available: AltStore PAL and Classic. AltStore PAL is the version you'll find in regions where Apple has been forced to allow sideloading, while Classic is the version you can install no matter where you are — but it requires a companion desktop app called AltServer. AltServer is available for both Windows and macOS, although on Windows you'll also need iTunes and iCloud installed (make sure they come directly from Apple, not the Microsoft Store).
Start by plugging your iPhone into your Mac or PC with a cable — unlock it and confirm you trust the computer before continuing. Turn on Wi-Fi Sync for the device in iTunes or Finder if the option isn't already enabled. Now all you need to do is click the AltServer icon, select Install AltStore and choose your device — it will ask you to sign in to your Apple Developer account. If you've forgotten your credentials, here's how to change your Apple Account password. Now open Settings and go to General, then VPN & Device Management and mark your Apple Developer account as trusted. Enable Developer Mode in Settings > Privacy & Security.
Once you see AltStore on your home screen, you can add external sources to it. You can also install apps downloaded from other sources. Sign in with the same account, then open the IPA file in Files and select AltStore from the Share menu — it will identify the app and sideload it. AltServer needs to be running on your computer when installing apps this way, with your iPhone or iPad either connected by cable or on the same Wi-Fi network. With a paid Apple Developer account, you get a much higher limit for sideloading apps.
How to sideload apps on iOS without a PC
If you don't want to rely on a computer so often for sideloading, there are a few alternatives — including one from AltStore itself. With AltStore Classic open on your iPhone, tap Settings and sign in to your Apple Developer account. Then, scroll down and tap Set up Remote AltServer and follow the in-app instructions. But here's the catch: you'll also need the LocalDevVPN app installed and active on your iOS device; otherwise, the remote server won't connect. Once all of this is set up, you'll be able to sideload apps from AltStore without a computer nearby.
Another option is to use SideStore, which works almost exactly the same way as AltStore. The difference is that you can use SideInstaller to complete all the steps on your phone, so no computer is needed at all. But it only works on iOS 27 because it takes advantage of a new feature for trusting developer accounts wirelessly. Similarly, you also need to have an Apple Developer account and the LocalDevVPN app installed.
Of course, if you live in the EU, Japan or Brazil, none of these workarounds are really necessary for sideloading. It's usually as simple as opening an app marketplace website, hitting install and then allowing the app to run in Settings.

articles.title: Pedestal AI raises $4.7 million to agentify the supply chain | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Delivery supply chains are the lifeblood of contemporary businesses — and a new startup is betting that purpose-built AI agents can make them run a lot more smoothly.
On Tuesday, Pedestal AI emerged from stealth with $4.7 million in seed funding. The company’s goal is to use agentic AI to make supply chains faster and more reliable — a plan that’s already brought them together with Fortune 500 companies and some of the largest shipping firms in the world.
The seed round was led by Eclipse, with participation from RRE, Converge VC, Timescale Ventures, and VitalStage. Pedestal says the funding will be used to expand its product and engineering time, grow the marketing organization, and support additional deployments.
In practice, much of Pedestal’s work is about removing friction from the shipping process — with agentic technology used as a means to that end. In one case, the company reduced missed deliveries for a major furniture company by 20% by deploying agents to take on some of the work that drivers were supposed to do. The agentic system they built would call customers 30 minutes before a delivery and collect any special instructions; if the call didn’t go through, a text would be sent from a separate system. Along the way, the deployment collected a wealth of data about friction points in the process, which could be used to optimize the system even further.
CEO Raj Aggarwal says contemporary AI systems are particularly useful for dealing with that data. “The challenge is that the data is messy and it’s constantly changing,” Aggarwal told TechCrunch. “It’s disparate because it sits in so many legacy systems. That’s what makes it hard.”
Supply chain AI has become a particularly hot space in recent months as alumni from autonomous driving teams look to launch their own startups. The supply chain startup Atomic, launched by a team of Tesla alumni, came out of stealth in 2025 with an emphasis on streamlining inventory. Another venture called Loop was launched by Uber alums to focus on predictive analytics.
As Aggarwal sees it, deliveries are particularly well-suited to training reinforcement learning systems. Because of their high volumes and easily measured outcomes, it’s easy to fine-tune contemporary AI systems toward what’s working and away from what isn’t.
Perhaps most importantly, it’s the kind of problem that can have an immediate effect on a client’s bottom line, making it easy to justify the expense.
“If you can get it right,” he told TechCrunch, “you can have really big impact.”

articles.title: The MacBook Neo is receiving a rare $50 discount ahead of Black Friday
articles.text:
If you’re looking for a new laptop or a gift for the student in your life, you can save $50 on the MacBook Neo at several retailers, in both storage sizes and all four colors. The 256GB model is currently discounted to $649 (Amazon, Best Buy, Target), while the 512GB model with Touch ID is down to $749 (Amazon, Best Buy, Target). None of the retailers currently list an end date for the discount, which is the biggest price drop we’ve seen since Apple raised the laptop’s MSRP by $100 in July in response to the ongoing RAM crisis.
The MacBook Neo is receiving a rare $50 discount ahead of Black Friday
While $50 might not feel like much, it brings the laptop closer to its original launch price.
Apple’s budget-friendly MacBook leverages the A18 Pro processor, a chip originally found in the iPhone 16 Pro, to keep costs down. Both the 256GB and 512GB models feature 8GB of memory, and my colleague Antonio G. Di Benedetto was impressed by the vivid 13-inch screen and speakers, the latter of which are better than those in many cheap (and even midrange) Windows laptops. The Neo isn’t super performant, especially in terms of storage speed and total memory, but it’s great for everyday tasks, casual use, and students.

articles.title: The Hidden Features Every Google Maps User Should Know About - Engadget
articles.text:
The hidden features every Google Maps user should know about
Maps has more tricks than you’ve tapped.
Most of us use Google Maps the same way day in and day out — we type in an address, follow the instructions and arrive at our destination. But the app also offers a lot of useful tools that aren't as easily accessible as telling it where to go. If you want to set a reminder for when to leave or ensure your music is uninterrupted while still getting the step-by-step instructions, there are settings you can change to make that happen. You can also turn Google Maps into a much more useful tool if you tell it what type of car you have, or specify your route settings all so you can get customized recommendations.
None of these features require a new app or a subscription, either. They are built directly into Google Maps, and you can get to them with a little bit of digging around, especially when you know where to look.
Travel the way you want by specifying your car and route
There's a feature within Google Maps that lets you specify what car you're driving. The make and model don't matter as much as what type of engine it has, letting you choose between gas, diesel, hybrid and electric. With this info, the app can tailor routing decisions to your car's needs.
For EV and plug-in hybrid owners, this feature is worth considering because you can tell Google Maps exactly what type of plug or adapter your car requires. This allows Maps to automatically surface compatible charging stations. You can find this setting in Settings > Your vehicles. Once set, you can search for charging stations along your route, and the app will signal those that will work with your specific car.
Route preferences deserve the same attention. The app's settings make it possible to toggle options to avoid tolls, ferries or even highways. This is useful if you'd rather take the scenic (or cheaper) route or if you wish to avoid the freeway at its higher speeds. To turn the feature on, go to Settings > Navigation, and you'll find all toggles under Route options. One thing that will save you time in the long run is setting or changing your home address on Google Maps so you can jump straight to your custom directions with a single tap. If you have your Gemini assistant enabled, you can even say "navigate home" and it will set the route for you.
Don't be late again with the help of reminders
Running late is rarely about the drive itself, but more about leaving at the wrong time. Unless an accident has delayed your journey, you probably left home late in accordance with your predicted arrival time — Google Maps is that good at estimating when you'll arrive based on your chosen route.
Well, you can use Google Maps on iPhone and its "Set a reminder to leave" feature to receive an alert telling you when to head out so you're not late for appointments. You can set an arrive-by time (or a leave-by time) for your destination under Directions > transportation mode and then tap the three-dot menu and select Set a reminder to leave > Depart or Arrive > set the time > Done. Maps will now notify you when to leave. On Android, things are a little different; to get the same results requires Google Calendar to set the reminder by creating an event with the appointment's date and time while adding the destination to the location field.
This feature shines best in busy cities where traffic on the same stretch of road can vary dramatically between a Monday afternoon and a Friday evening. For anyone juggling back-to-back meetings, school pickups and a million extracurricular activities, these reminders remove the need to check the app constantly. It's a quiet but dependable feature, and it's equally useful if you're planning on using public transport.
Get directions while keeping your music uninterrupted
If you've ever had Spotify, a book or a podcast cut out midway to announce an upcoming exit, you know how annoying that can be. Thankfully, there's an easy fix if you'd like to silence Google Maps: you simply have to turn off the "Play voice over Bluetooth" setting, a fine way to improve your Android Auto experience. This will stop Google Maps from interrupting your music over your car's speakers, while still giving you visual turn-by-turn guidance on screen. The voice telling you to turn left or right will come from your phone rather than your car's speakers. It's a small adjustment that will make a big difference, especially if you drive in the city a lot and need to change direction often. To do this, go to your profile, scroll down to Settings and go to Navigation. The feature's toggle will be available up top, under Sound & Voice.
One cool perk that's worth knowing about when you're using Android Auto is that when you're parked at your destination or somewhere for a rest, you can take a breather and play games directly on an Android Auto screen. That could make the wait during your kid's next practice session a little more entertaining.

articles.title: Apple vừa cập nhật "Face ID" cho iPhone Duo
articles.text:
Bản thử nghiệm mới của iOS 27.3 bổ sung 2 tuỳ chọn mà người dùng chiếc iPhone gập đầu tiên đã chờ từ lúc máy lên kệ.
Apple vừa phát hành bản thử nghiệm thứ hai của iOS 27.3 cho nhà phát triển. Với iPhone Duo, bản cập nhật này thêm khả năng mở khoá bằng khuôn mặt qua camera trước và một tuỳ chọn khoá máy ngay khi người dùng gập màn hình lại.
Mở khoá bằng camera trước, nhưng không phải Face ID thật
iPhone Duo ra mắt chỉ với cảm biến vân tay Touch ID, không có Face ID. Bản beta mới thêm lựa chọn thứ hai: mở khoá bằng nhận diện khuôn mặt qua camera trước, bật trong phần Touch ID & Mật mã (Touch ID & Passcode).
Cách này có nhiều giới hạn: chỉ dùng được ở màn hình khoá. Những thao tác nhạy cảm hơn như thanh toán bằng Apple Pay, thêm mật khẩu hay đăng nhập vẫn phải dùng Touch ID. Để dùng được camera, người dùng phải vừa xác thực bằng Touch ID hoặc mã khoá trong thời gian gần. Sau khoảng 45 phút không dùng máy, iPhone Duo sẽ đòi Touch ID trở lại.
Lý do Apple không đưa Face ID thật lên máy nằm ở độ mỏng. iPhone Duo chỉ dày 5,2 mm khi mở ra, nên không đủ chỗ cho cụm cảm biến Face ID. Cách mở khoá bằng camera trước thông thường là phương án bù lại, và các giới hạn bảo mật kể trên cho thấy Apple coi nó kém an toàn hơn.
Gập máy lại là khoá
Tính năng khoá khi gập nằm trong phần Màn hình & Độ sáng (Display & Brightness) của ứng dụng Cài đặt. Khi bật, iPhone Duo sẽ khoá lại lúc người dùng gập máy, thay vì chuyển nội dung sang màn hình ngoài như hiện nay.
Thiết lập mặc định này từng gây khó chịu cho một số người dùng. Federico Viticci, người đánh giá iPhone Duo, cho biết ông liên tục gập máy lại và chờ nó tự khoá, giống như đóng một cuốn sách hay gập một chiếc laptop. Trước đó, ông phải tự tạo một tự động hoá đơn giản trong ứng dụng Phím tắt (Shortcuts) để máy khoá lại khi gập.
Ông cũng chỉ ra điều ngược lại: có lúc người dùng chỉ muốn chuyển từ màn hình trong sang màn hình ngoài nhỏ hơn, và việc phải xác thực lại bằng vân tay lúc đó rất phiền. Vì vậy Apple để đây là tuỳ chọn riêng, người dùng muốn giữ cách cũ vẫn giữ được.
Cả hai tính năng đang ở bản thử nghiệm cho nhà phát triển, nên cách hoạt động và tên gọi có thể thay đổi trước khi chính thức. Apple cho biết iOS 27.3 sẽ phát hành rộng rãi vào tháng 12.

articles.title: Proton's Lumo, a privacy-focused alternative to ChatGPT and Claude, arrives on desktop | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Proton, the privacy-focused tech company offering alternatives to Google’s and Microsoft’s tools for email, productivity apps, password management, cloud storage, and more, is now bringing its AI app Lumo to personal computers. On Tuesday, the company launched Lumo Desktop for Windows, macOS, and Linux, allowing users to leverage its AI to carry out local tasks on their computer involving connected apps, personal files, and other automations.
The app is designed to offer users more control over their personal data, as consumer AI technology becomes focused more on AI agents that can perform tasks on users’ behalf, rather than just answering questions.
Already, the major model makers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and others, offer desktop tools for working with their AI technologies, but doing so invites increased risk to users’ personal data. Only this week, for instance, Apple announced it was addressing those privacy concerns with tightened security settings for apps that request Full Disk Access, as the AI desktop apps do.
Proton’s idea is to offer a set of tools that let its AI access connected apps, files, and folders and automate tasks, but with more personalization over how much access the AI has. The company says users can choose which actions the AI agent takes that will need to request their approval, and it vows that the conversations and information from connected apps and files are never used to serve personalized ads or train AI models.
The new app includes a variety of connectors that support local tools, like file-system access, shell execution, and browser content fetching, as well as Proton’s email app and other third-party services, including Confluence, Dropbox, and Jira.
The connectors also support local and remote MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, which AI agents use to access external data sources.
Proton says that users can decide for each connector which actions Lumo can perform automatically, which require approval, and which are blocked entirely. Users can also turn individual tools off from the Tools menu in their conversation.
In addition, users can set up their own scheduled tasks, where each has its own set of permissions, in terms of what can be handled automatically and what requires approval.
Proton notes that it uses encryption to ensure that only users can read their chat history, not the company. The company also says it keeps no server-side logs, and the limited data it does store is protected under Swiss privacy law. The data is hosted on European infrastructure, outside the scope of the U.S. CLOUD Act, which specifies how law enforcement agencies access data held by cloud service providers.
The company says it’s investing in its infrastructure, with its first Nvidia B300 cluster built on Open Compute Project (OCP) standards now going live in Switzerland.
Similar to other AI apps, Lumo’s desktop app supports Skills, which lets users save instructions, templates, and reference files that Lumo can reuse across their conversations. (An earlier version of this, Custom Lumos, will now be migrated to the Skills format.)

articles.title: Nvidia’s Q3 earnings hit the mark, without mentioning the whole Jensen Huang thing
articles.text:
Interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress announced the company’s Q3 earnings on Tuesday, without initially mentioning former CEO Jensen Huang or the details of his departure, or possible attempt at a return. On the earnings call accompanying the release, board chair Harvey Jones kicked things off by saying the board “does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO,” and that “we will not be addressing or taking questions on today’s call regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation,” before Kress started with her comments on the results.
Nvidia’s Q3 earnings hit the mark, without mentioning the whole Jensen Huang thing
Nvidia’s Q3 revenue has more than doubled, with income from data centers up 110 percent from last year, to $107.6 billion.
As it predicted in the last financial update, Nvidia is now on the list of companies that have pulled in over $100 billion in a single quarter, with revenues of $115.8 billion, up 103 percent from the same period last year and higher than its expectation of $108 billion. This quarter’s figures include data center revenues of $107.6 billion, which were up 110 percent, and edge computing (which includes the consumer gaming PC business and devices like the new RTX Spark laptops) revenue of $8.2 billion, up 42 percent.
The company reported $65.3 billion in profit, a new record.
“Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” said Colette Kress, interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer of NVIDIA. “Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater.”
In the fourth quarter, Nvidia expects revenues of $130 billion.
Update, November 17th: Added comments from Nvidia’s earnings call.

articles.title: Suno adds AI video to its music app, with filters for artists' faces
articles.text:
AI music company Suno has launched Visuals, which makes images and video clips of up to 15 seconds to match users’ songs, including lyric videos that lip-sync. It is on the web now, uses separate credits, and comes with filters meant to block likenesses of artists, public figures and copyrighted work.
AI music company Suno has launched Visuals, a tool that makes images and short videos to go with users’ songs, it announced on Tuesday. Users can create lyric videos, album art and clips of up to 15 seconds. It is on the web now, with iOS and Android apps due in the next few weeks.
Suno says its video model is built around music. Clips follow a song’s structure, pick up on its lyrics and lip-sync to them. Users can start from Suno’s own characters or upload an image, then extend and edit clips with text prompts.
Visuals runs on its own credits, bought separately from song credits. It follows Suno’s Speech tool, launched in October for spoken audio such as poems and meditations.
New filters will block prompts and uploads that try to show specific artists, public figures or copyrighted characters, Suno says. Videos will also carry hidden watermarks before they can be shared outside Suno. ByteDance added similar guardrails to its Seedance video tool in March.
“This means that prompts that work on other video platforms may not work on Suno and that’s by design,” the company wrote.
Those guardrails come as Suno fights fresh legal battles. Last week, Elvis Presley’s music owners and Eminem’s publisher sued Suno, and the Presley suit claims it misused his voice.
Suno has been trying to look more legitimate. It launched music models trained on licensed songs from Warner and BMG in September, and plans audio watermarks for its tracks. Investors valued the company at $5.4B in June.

articles.title: Xiaomi's 18 Pro Series Can Generate Vibe-Coded Apps For Its Tiny Rear Display - Engadget
articles.text:
Xiaomi's 18 Pro series can generate vibe-coded apps for its tiny rear display
The cameras don’t seem to reach the dizzying heights of last year’s 17 Ultra.
Xiaomi's premium smartphone series has been in great form in recent years. Alongside last year's 17 Ultra (and its Leica-collab camera), it launched its own passport-shaped foldable, the technically impressive 18 Fold, just before Apple debuted the iPhone Duo.
Its new phones, the Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, combine a more advanced rear display with some of the company's latest innovations found on the 17 Ultra and its foldables. Naturally, because it's 2026, that includes a serving of AI assistance and generative AI, but Xiaomi brought some genuinely smart ideas to the latter. The Pro series is launching in more regions this year, including the UK and other parts of Western Europe, but still won't come to the US. The 18 Pro Max is priced at £1400 (roughly $1,850) and the 18 Pro at £1,199 (around $1,580), continuing this year's upward trajectory of smartphone prices. Both are priced higher than Xiaomi's flagship (and my favorite camera phone), the 17 Ultra.
The Xiaomi 18 Pro Max has a 6.9-inch main display and a slightly larger 2.9-inch rear display. The 18 Pro, meanwhile, has a 6.40-inch screen with a 2.7-inch rear display. The Pro Max model also features Snapdragon's new 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chip, with up to 16 gigs of RAM, while the 18 Pro has a (still powerful) Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 with 12GB of RAM.
There are also battery capacity differences between the two phones. The Xiaomi 18 Pro has a 6,000mAh cell with 90W max charging, but if you're demanding more battery life, the Pro Max has a larger 7,050mAh battery and 100W fast charging.
The hardware feels decidedly premium, complemented by a couple of vivid color options, including a gorgeous Velvet Red finish last seen on Xiaomi's latest foldable. Both phones will also come in Black, White and Cosmic Blue colors. Even if you choose the vivid red or blue models, it's the small back display that catches the eye first.
The Back Display
The Back Display uses the same display tech as the Xiaomi 18 Pro series' screen, peaking at 4,000-nit brightness and up to 120Hz refresh rates, though chances of seeing those upper limits are probably few and far between. Both the back display and camera array are protected with a single Corning Gorilla Glass Victus cover, making a surprisingly busy back look a little more cohesive.
The Back Display's functions fall into two main categories. First, like the flip foldables we've seen in recent years, it works as a display for the phone's primary cameras. The back display's viewfinder automatically switches to ultra-wide if it spots three or more people in the shot, but otherwise it's a stripped-down version of the camera app. While it makes sense, given the smaller screen space for buttons and modes, it relegates many shooting modes and features to the main camera app on the phone's main screen.
Alongside the notifications and information feeds we've seen on phones like Samsung's Z Flip series and Motorola's Razr phones, including calls, maps and weather, Xiaomi adds a pin-to-back function that lets you attach text and images for quick reference. The company suggests pinning boarding passes and QR codes, but you could also add a cute pic of family or pets. It's also the first rear display to support apps like Spotify, YouTube Music and Google Maps – hopefully more apps will join those. Xiaomi said Gemini Live can run on the rear display, but I haven't been able to get it to work on my 18 Pro yet.
The new feature on this year's Back Display lets you program your own mini apps, similar to how you can program the iPhone's recent AI-infused Shortcuts. Using GenAI, you can describe a lightweight app or function, and the Xiaomi 18 Pro will attempt to make it a reality. It's a clever way to sidestep the difficulty of getting app developers on board with niche screen sizes and proportions. Xiaomi promises over 50 preset apps at launch, although the selection was much more limited on the Xiaomi 17 Pro I've been using.
It's not about making dense, full-size apps, but rather simple, single-purpose (interactive) widgets. There's something to this idea, but I couldn't quite get apps to behave or look the way I wanted. One idea: a faux wallpaper that would generate screen cracks and glitches when touched. Regardless of how many times I asked the phone not to include an on-screen crack counter, ruining the appeal of my lame 'prank', subsequent vibe-coded builds still featured a counter.
I also tried to create a guess-the-flag quiz, but it seemed to lean heavily on the 25 or so countries that most of us could answer, easily. When I asked it to increase the flag range by 100 more, the phone struggled to generate a new mini app, even though I assumed it was an easy expansion of the initial premise. There are some smart implementations, including a button to 'polish' the idea you wrote to make it more palatable to generative AI.
It's a little sluggish to both refine and generate these mini-apps, especially if you've dipped your toe into genAI coding elsewhere, which is usually pretty swift. The feature requires an internet connection to work and it's not entirely clear whether they're generated on-device, which might explain slower processing.
Wallpaper options for the tiny rear display also include AI Group photo wallpapers, which I'm less sold on, which combine two different subjects into a group photo. You can even create composite portraits of celebrities and fictional characters – maybe this just isn't for me. I'll go back to my flag guessing.
The primary screens on both phones feature Xiaomi's Privacy Display technology, which can be assigned to toggle on with specific apps (like banking apps, photo galleries, dating apps and more). This extends to notifications and even floating windows and split-screen versions of those apps — it's a better implementation of the privacy display tech we saw on Samsung's Galaxy S26 Ultra. In settings, you can even enable a gaze detection mode that notifies you if the front-facing camera recognizes someone possibly peering at your phone. The 18 Pro will notify you on-screen or with a more subtle vibration.
The cameras
Cameras are once again a priority for Xiaomi. Both phones have dual 200-megapixel camera systems, with Leica Summilux lenses. The 18 Pro Max has a 200MP Light Fusion 960L primary sensor with LOFIC technology, which delivers more dynamic range to protect highlights and boost low-light performance. The 18 Pro, however, uses the same 200MP Light Fusion 960 sensor, minus the LOFIC part. Both have an f/1.67 lens and optical image stabilization.
The periscope telephoto is also 200MP, with an f/2.4 lens, OIS and 3.2x optical zoom, extending to 12.8x in-sensor cropped zoom. There's a 50MP ultrawide too, separately nestled below the other two cameras. This makes for a more sensible-looking camera array alongside the back display, the very opposite of Motorola's tryptophobia-inducing Signature 17.
I've been testing the 18 Pro's cameras for only a few days (and the 18 Pro Max is arriving today, so I'll have updated impressions soon). Performance doesn't reach the high expectations set by last year's 17 Ultra, with its massive 1-inch sensor. While daylight shots and macro landscapes remain crisp, the standard Pro often struggled to capture moving subjects and low-light scenes. The Pro Max-exclusive LOFIC sensor could bridge that gap, however, so I'll update this story if it does.
Leica's Essential Moments is an enjoyable shooting mode in the camera app, evolving from a single-camera mode to multiple styles and even lens options. It's a little different from the Leica camera simulations on Xiaomi's flagships last year. Powered by Xiaomi's own large model photography engine, the shooting mode applies one of three Leica-inspired color grades. You can also shoot through two "classic lens" simulations based on 35mm and 75mm lenses. Xiaomi has distilled it down to three styles, and I've always liked the old-school CCD tones of Leica cameras. As I've said in other reviews and hands-ons, Xiaomi and Leica seem to have nailed this, including a monochrome mode (which, again, is great), while keeping it curated to just three distinct looks.
There are all the other shooting modes you'd expect, too, with Xiaomi's pro shooting mode another standout. Focus peaking and exposure highlights are baked in, and you can refine your own filter parameters, including adding noise grain and hue.
For now, Xiaomi's 17 Ultra remains its true photography flagship, but the 18 Pro series still delivers impressive results and, crucially, a fun shooting experience. In the UK, both phones are available to order from Xiaomi and Amazon.

articles.title: Giải bài toán bản quyền và chi phí công nghệ cho doanh nghiệp Việt
articles.text:
Việc lựa chọn Windows, Office hay Cloud đòi hỏi cân bằng giữa tuân thủ bản quyền và tối ưu chi phí. MM Technology (Công ty TNHH Công Nghệ Mật Mã) – đối tác chiến lược của Microsoft, Google, Zoho sẵn sàng đồng hành cùng doanh nghiệp.
Mua phần mềm không còn đơn giản là chọn sản phẩm
Windows nào phù hợp với máy tính đang sử dụng? Nên chọn Office vĩnh viễn hay Microsoft 365? Muốn chuyển sang môi trường làm việc trên đám mây, nền tảng công nghệ nào sẽ phù hợp hơn?
Đây là những câu hỏi tưởng chừng đơn giản nhưng có thể trở nên phức tạp khi mỗi sản phẩm lại có nhiều phiên bản, phạm vi sử dụng và hình thức cấp phép khác nhau.
Bài toán không chỉ là "mua bản quyền", mà là mua phiên bản nào và mua thế nào cho phù hợp. Khi doanh nghiệp chú trọng tuân thủ, phần mềm cần có nguồn gốc, giấy phép rõ ràng và đáp ứng chi phí vận hành.
MM Technology giúp doanh nghiệp lựa chọn từ nhu cầu thực tế
Thay vì bắt đầu bằng câu hỏi "nên mua sản phẩm nào?", MM Technology tiếp cận từ nhu cầu sử dụng, số lượng người dùng, thiết bị, môi trường CNTT hiện tại và ngân sách dự kiến.
Từ đó, đội ngũ MM Technology tư vấn phiên bản, số lượng giấy phép và phương án phù hợp để cân bằng giữa yêu cầu sử dụng, yếu tố bản quyền và chi phí đầu tư.
MM Technology tư vấn phần mềm và giải pháp bản quyền cho doanh nghiệp.
Windows và Office bản quyền
Với nhóm sản phẩm Microsoft, MM Technology cung cấp các lựa chọn bản quyền phổ biến gồm:
– Windows 11 và Windows 11 Pro: đáp ứng các nhu cầu sử dụng hệ điều hành trên máy tính cá nhân và môi trường làm việc.
– Windows Server: phục vụ nhu cầu xây dựng và vận hành hạ tầng máy chủ.
– Office Home: bộ ứng dụng Office dành cho nhu cầu sử dụng cơ bản.
– Office Home & Business: hướng đến người dùng có nhu cầu làm việc và sử dụng Office trong môi trường kinh doanh.

articles.title: Nike’s new air sole technology can mix soft and firm cushioning
articles.text:
In 2024, Nike announced its Air Max 1000 that were manufactured using a 3D-printing process resulting in a shoe that had a uniform silhouette but varying areas of support and flexibility throughout. The company is now doing something similar with its iconic air-filled soles using its new Tuned Air technology. While previously the level of cushioning in Nike Air shoes was uniform across the entire sole, a new manufacturing process can produce multiple air pockets with varying levels of cushioning and stability.
Nike’s new air sole technology can mix soft and firm cushioning
The first shoes with Nike’s new Tuned Air technology will be available for runners starting in late 2027.
Nike has been putting air pockets into its shoes for nearly 50 years as a way to increase comfort and cushioning while making them lighter. Its air pockets have even found their way into apparel as a way to improve insulation by trapping body heat, but Nike plans to use its new Tuned Air technology as a way to customize the cushioning experience in its shoes and tailor them to specific athletes and sports. The first shoes featuring the technology are expected to arrive in late 2027 and will be targeted at runners.
While one of Nike’s earliest successes was track shoes with a grip design inspired by a waffle iron, the company credits the “vibrant colors on magazine covers” as the inspiration for its latest shoe technology. A Tuned Air sole is manufactured using a “proprietary digital print and selective lamination process” where an ink is applied in specific patterns that define where the layers bond to each other. This process can be used to create internal pockets in an unlimited combination of shapes and sizes, and by fine-tuning how much air is in each of those pockets, some parts of the sole can feel firmer while others feel softer.
The Tuned Air technology will not only allow Nike to highly customize the fit and feel of air sole shoes for different sports, it will also help keep the benefits of the custom tuning consistent across different sizes. The new manufacturing process will also help reduce the amount of time it takes Nike to go from a concept for a new shoe to a final design ready for production. “Prototypes that once took three weeks can now be made in three days,” the company claims in a release today. That gives Nike’s designers more time to refine new shoes, and more opportunity to experiment.

articles.title: AI models can be tricked into identifying civilians as military targets by telling them it's a game | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Some AI models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and other leading AI labs could be easily tricked into identifying targets for military strikes — even if they include civilians or locations like schools — simply by being told they’re playing a game, according to a new research report by Vals.
Vals, a San Francisco-based AI evaluation startup, tested whether leading AI models could be manipulated into participating in autonomous warfare. Researchers used simulated scenarios and a combination of generated and real imagery from Ukraine and Iran to see if the AI models would mark targets in drone and satellite imagery.
The models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, and other companies frequently identified potential targets in drone and satellite imagery, including civilians and surrendering soldiers. When the models refused to cooperate, researchers were able to jailbreak them by claiming the battlefield scenarios were part of a game.
The findings come amid growing fears about the immediate risks posed by AI, beyond the existential threats associated with artificial general intelligence.
Earlier this year, Anthropic became embroiled in a dispute with the Department of Defense after it told the agency it could not use Anthropic’s technology for mass surveillance of Americans or autonomous warfare. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has insisted that today’s AI systems aren’t reliable enough to make life-or-death decisions without a human in the loop. Meanwhile, the Pentagon argued it should be able to deploy the technology for any lawful military purpose.
The new research raises further questions about whether AI companies are capable of preventing their models from being used in warfare.
Ironically, AI models from Anthropic performed the worst in these simulated scenarios. But none of the models performed particularly well. None of the researchers’ requests were blocked by a safety classifier, and refusals were uncommon. Even when models did refuse, they often complied after being told they were playing a game.
Anthropic spokesperson Eduardo Maia Silva told TechCrunch the company appreciates Vals’ report, recommendations, and collaboration, and acknowledged that the outcomes were not acceptable.
“The examples in the report are very clearly against our rules and we have banned and will ban users when we see this behavior,” according to an emailed company statement sent by Silva. “Even for authorized settings, Anthropic has long been firm that today’s frontier AI systems are not reliable enough to power fully autonomous weapons.”
Anthropic told TechCrunch that its teams were already developing additional safeguards before the report was published and that those measures would be in place soon. Anthropic is also expanding its own testing and enhancing safeguards and enforcement to address any gaps it finds.
OpenAI spokesperson Nate Evans told TechCrunch the company prohibits using its public models to facilitate violence or for unapproved national security purposes, including in the scenarios Vals simulated.
“We actively detect and disrupt misuse, including by suspending accounts that violate our policies,” OpenAI said in an emailed statement. “We’re also developing additional safeguards for our public models against misuse involving drones and drone software.”
Vals notes in the report that the models were never asked to directly make strike decisions, a task the researchers said the models would typically refuse. That doesn’t mean their outputs couldn’t have dire or fatal consequences in the real world. For instance, targeting information could be used by autonomous weapons systems.
In some scenarios, the models were asked to report whether people were visible. Positive reports were followed by simulated strikes and the models would see the consequences.
The report relies on commercial models from frontier AI labs, not the models those companies might provide to the military. It’s not clear whether the additional safeguards would apply to military use, though.
Vals also noted that technical challenges, including latency and limited onboard computing capacity, make it difficult to use general-purpose AI models for live drone targeting. Those constraints make their deployment in combat less of an immediate threat.
A more immediate threat, the researchers say, is that AI models could be used to annotate battlefield footage at scale, producing training data for autonomous targeting systems.
For instance, researchers relied on real satellite imagery of an Iranian school that was bombed by the U.S. in February 2026, killing more than 150 civilians. Bloomberg later reported that an “overreliance on AI” contributed to the strike. In Vals’ testing, models frequently marked the school, which sat next to a military complex, as a strike target, with Claude Opus 5.5 selecting the school in 69% of ordinary trials and 72% of game-framed trials.
Anthropic no longer has an active Pentagon contract, but other companies, including SpaceXAI, OpenAI, and Google do. A recent Congressional Research Service report found that the Pentagon is not known to be using any frontier AI model in autonomous weapons systems directly.
TechCrunch has also reached out to Meta, Google, Thinking Machines Lab, and SpaceXAI for comment.

articles.title: Uber Eats starts drone deliveries with Zipline in Houston
articles.text:
Zipline has started delivering Uber Eats orders by drone in Houston, the first launch under the companies’ August partnership. Dallas comes next, and the pair are aiming for 1 million drone deliveries a day by 2029.
Uber Eats customers in Houston can now get food delivered by drone, Zipline announced on Tuesday. Customers pick “by drone” on the Uber Eats home screen, and a Zipline aircraft brings the order to their door. Dallas is next, followed by more US cities.
It is the first launch under the companies’ August partnership, which aims for 1 million drone deliveries a day by 2029. Uber also agreed to invest in Zipline, but did not say how much.
Zipline’s aircraft fly at up to 70mph and carry up to 8 pounds over 10 miles. They stay about 330 feet up and lower orders to the ground on a tether, which Zipline says keeps the noise down.
“Being able to reach people’s homes autonomously in under 10 minutes opens up a whole new opportunity for Uber Eats and its customers,” said Uber’s autonomous delivery head, Aaron Emrich.
Zipline says more than 80% of its orders are new business for restaurants, not orders they would have got anyway. It has made 1 million deliveries in the Dallas area alone.
Houston is not new ground for Zipline. In April, it opened early access there for the first 5,000 residents through its own app.
The drone delivery race is speeding up. Zipline raised $1.5B at a $21.5B valuation this month, as Walmart agreed to add 300 drone sites. Amazon plans to offer drone delivery in nearly 500 US cities and towns by the end of the year.
Food delivery rivals are moving too. DoorDash has unveiled its own drones, and Irish startup Manna is building a US drone factory in Oklahoma.
