articles.title: 5 important Bose headphone settings that need to be manually turned on - Engadget
articles.text:
5 important Bose headphone settings that need to be manually turned on
Pairing your Bose headphones is just the beginning. A few small tweaks in the companion app's settings can make your headphones feel more like yours.
Bose has made some of the most popular headphones around for years, but even if you've been using them for a while, you may not be getting everything you can out of yours. The company's headphones are perfectly capable of producing great sound right out of the box, but some of their best features actually have to be activated manually. Whether there's something you always wished your headphones could do or you just want to see if they can perform even better, it's worth exploring settings like an equalizer, multi-connection support, noise canceling, shortcuts to your favorite features, or sidetone settings.
Keep in mind that not every pair of Bose headphones will have access to all of these settings. Newer QuietComfort models are upgraded in all the right places, offering a few unique features, while first-generation QuietComfort Ultra and QuietComfort headphones lack some of those features. You'll also need to download the Bose app to tweak anything beyond their basic settings, as the controls on the headphones themselves are pretty minimal.
Adjust the equalizer for better sound
One useful feature on compatible Bose headphones is the equalizer (EQ). Like with any piece of audio equipment, the equalizer lets you modify different sound frequencies to your taste, like adjusting the audio quality in Apple Music, letting you pump up the bass or improving the high end so it's brighter. Reviews often call out Bose for boosting bass too much out of the box, so it may be a good idea to try turning it down a touch before making other adjustments.
Bose's equalizer only lets you change volume across three bands — bass, mid and treble — but that's plenty for most users without making it too complex. There are also preset options to choose from if you want to take Bose's recommendations or pick one to start with and customize your profile from there. You'll find the equalizer on the home screen of the Bose app, under EQ.
Set up multipoint connections for (relatively) seamless device switching
One of the more annoying aspects of using Bluetooth headphones is having to disconnect and reconnect them whenever you want to switch from one device to another. Bluetooth multipoint lets Bluetooth devices connect to multiple sources at once, so you can switch between them without disconnecting and reconnecting. Compatible Bose headphones have this feature, but you have to enable it in the app.
You'll find Bluetooth multipoint in the Settings section of the app, under Bluetooth Connections. Just toggle it on, and you'll be able to connect your headphones to two different audio sources. To switch devices, pause the audio on one and press play on the other, or swap between them in the app if the switch doesn't happen. Like basically everything to do with Bluetooth, multipoint connection doesn't always work perfectly, but it's extremely convenient when it does.
Choose a noise-canceling mode or create your own
Bose features some serious pros of using noise-canceling headphones. You can choose from a few modes to adjust how noise-canceling works, with newer models adding more modes. QuietComfort Ultra headphones turn on in Quiet mode by default, but if you find an option you like better, you can set the app to remember the last mode used through the app's Settings menu.
Under the Modes menu in the app, you'll find at least two different noise-canceling presets, depending on which headphones you have. Quiet (full noise cancellation) and Aware (full transparency) are available on the QuietComfort Ultra headphones. In newer headphones, Immersion mode aims to replicate the experience of music being played from a stage in front of you, and Cinema mode enhances dialogue clarity while you're watching movies and TV. You can also define multiple custom modes by choosing which specific noise-canceling features to activate.
Add a shortcut for your most-used feature
Many Bose headphones let you customize their controls, though the specifics will obviously depend on which model you own. QuietComfort Ultra headphones have a touch-sensitive strip, and older headphone models offer the Action Button, both of which can activate your chosen shortcut.
To set the behavior of the custom control, check the Shortcut option in the app. Depending on your model, this will let you choose from a few options, including hearing the battery level as it changes, changing the Immersive Audio mode and switching between previously connected Bluetooth devices. For headphones, you can only set one, but some earbuds let you assign a different shortcut to each ear. If you don't use shortcuts and don't want to risk accidentally activating them, you can also turn them off completely in the app.
Change your Self Voice settings for clearer calls
A somewhat more niche feature comes in the form of Self Voice. If you've ever taken a call while wearing headphones, especially noise-canceling ones, you might be familiar with how strange it can be to hear your own voice muffled as you speak. By default, Bose headphones feed a certain amount of your own voice back to you to make speaking feel more natural, otherwise known as sidetone.
The Self Voice feature in the app lets you adjust just how much comes through, but you won't find it on the home screen. Instead, tap the Settings gear icon and look for Self Voice there, where you can set it to High, Medium or Low, or turn it off completely. As long as it's not turned off, Self Voice activates automatically during calls, so you don't need to manually toggle it on.

articles.title: Not even Sam Altman is safe from AI deepfakes on Instagram
articles.text:
Instagram is filled with people posting deepfaked content — including, as of late, from one of Meta’s most prominent executives.
Not even Sam Altman is safe from AI deepfakes on Instagram
Meta’s chief AI officer posted an AI video of a top competitor. It’s allowed under Meta’s AI policy.
Earlier in November, Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, shared a short clip to promote Muse, the company’s consumer AI agent. In the AI-generated clip, Wang, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, and Jolly, the anthropomorphic mascot of Muse, are on a four-way video call. When Altman joins the call he’s dressed like Jolly, wearing a furry hooded suit and face paint to look like the cutesy character. The clip is captioned “When the homies meet about openai product strategy,” a reference to the AI agent race and the recent popularity of Muse.
Just a few years ago, AI content portraying real people led to strong public statements rebuking the use of the technology to imitate humans. In some cases legal action was threatened. Now, AI content has become part of the texture of a new reality, especially on social media. Leading up to the midterm elections, for example, political groups ran millions of dollars’ worth of AI-generated ads attacking opponents.
Wang has been doing a lot of what some have described as “anti-PR” to promote Muse, tweeting hundreds of times and referring to more traditional marketers as “corposlops.” Still, a major tech executive posting an AI video of a competitor is notable, especially on a platform that’s been criticized recently over AI-generated content. After an AI-generated image of actress Mia Goth gained traction in October, the Pearl star’s representative told The Verge it was “incomprehensible” that Instagram allowed the image to spread instead of focusing on the “protection and integrity of a public figure’s likeness.” Other celebrities, including Scarlett Johansson, are regularly the subject of sexualized AI imagery; Meta has removed some accounts in the past that it found to be posing as someone else and using their likeness.
Meta requires AI-generated videos depicting people to be labeled as AI, like Wang’s post is. Static images, however, have no such requirement, meaning the AI image of Goth had no disclosure. To make matters worse, the image was shared by a fan account with a blue verification badge given by Instagram.
Reached for comment, Meta spokesperson Tracy Clayton noted that Wang’s post is labeled as AI content. Clayton also pointed out that Altman has made his likeness available for AI content generation, as when OpenAI launched its Sora app (and it was quickly flooded with fake Altman videos). OpenAI didn’t respond to requests for comment.

articles.title: Jensen Huang says he would be 'honored' if allowed to return as Nvidia CEO | TechCrunch
articles.text:
In the first public statement since his resignation, Nvidia founder Jensen Huang signaled his willingness to return as CEO if the board decides it is in the company’s best interest.
Huang’s statement, posted in full on X, reads as follows:
Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I’ve never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.
I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA. 
I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. 
Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO. 
Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.
Jensen
Huang resigned after reports of multiple affairs, including with a direct report and another with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who is suspected of working with Chinese intelligence services. Nvidia’s chip exports have faced intense scrutiny since the revelations, and Huang is scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1.
In Huang’s absence, Nvidia has formed a new executive committee to oversee export control compliance.
Still, many investors and employees associated with Nvidia have called for Huang to return as CEO, at least until an investigation can provide clearer evidence of guilt. An open letter circulated earlier this week attracted the signatures of more than 10,000 current and former Nvidia employees, as well as prominent tech figures like Elon Musk, Amjad Masad, and Travis Kalanick.
“We are concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process,” the letter reads. “If the Board believes his continued absence is necessary, provide a specific, evidence-based explanation of why it serves NVIDIA’s best interests.”
Still, many see such a return as unlikely. On Monday, an unnamed source on Nvidia’s board told The Washington Post there were no plans to reinstate Huang. There’s also significant resistance to the idea in Congress, where Huang still faces significant questions about his role in chip exports to China-linked firms.
Reached by Politico, one senator called Huang’s reinstatement “one of the worst ideas I’ve heard today.”

articles.title: Microsoft reveals that an old bug caused the massive outage that took its services offline - Engadget
articles.text:
Microsoft reveals that an old bug caused the massive outage that took its services offline
It was one of three root causes for the outage that affected business, hospitals, governments and other organizations worldwide.
Microsoft has revealed more details about the outage that took services like Outlook, Teams and Copilot 365 offline, affecting businesses, hospitals, law enforcement and other organizations around the world. Charles Lamanna, the company's EVP for Copilot and AI Agents, explained on X that there were three root causes for the outage.
He said that Microsoft typically maintains two network gateway systems that connect separate systems and allow data to pass between them. One of those gateways wasn't working for Microsoft Teams, and it overwhelmed the primary gateway. It also just so happened that nearly 14 percent of the capacity for that gateway was out of service due to an unrelated issue that happened the previous day. Those two factors caused that gateway to encounter a latent bug that's been in Microsoft's systems since July.
Together, the higher load that overwhelmed the gateway, the reduced server capacity and the latent bug led to a build up in traffic requests until Microsoft's servers gave out and stopped functioning. This all happened on a Thursday afternoon, during peak hours of use in the US.
The outage lasted for almost a full day. Microsoft worked on fixing the issue overnight, but the bug was months-old at that point, and the company was unable to simply do a rollback in order to quickly undo the changes it had caused. In addition, its servers were overwhelmed by waiting traffic after returning to service and became unresponsive again.
"We are deeply sorry for the impact to all our customers and recognize the impact that this has on their normal business & operations," Lamanna wrote on his post. These details are from Microsoft's preliminary post-incident report, and the company said it will release more details in the final report to be released later this week.

articles.title: ‘I own my mistakes’: Jensen Huang offers to return as Nvidia CEO
articles.text:
Jensen Huang says he would return as Nvidia’s chief executive if the board decides it wants him back. He made the offer in a written statement obtained by David Faber of CNBC on Tuesday. It is his first public comment since he resigned as chief executive on 12 November. CNBC’s Kif Leswing published the statement in full.
“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Huang said.
The statement landed hours before Nvidia reports third-quarter results, its first without him.
An apology to the board
Huang apologised to Nvidia’s directors and said he would cooperate with the board’s independent investigation.
“I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret,” he said.
He said he had seen an outpouring of calls for his return from Nvidia staff, investors, business partners and customers. Many still contact him directly, he said. An open letter asking the board to reinstate him now has more than 180,000 signatures, CNBC reported. President Donald Trump said on Monday that he would not mind Huang coming back.
Huang also wrote about his own story. He came to the US 53 years ago. He called becoming an American citizen one of the proudest moments of his life. He described Nvidia as his life’s work.
Where the board stands
Huang resigned days after admitting to an affair, CNBC reported. News reports alleged affairs with Nvidia employees and with Alice Huang, who worked for a customer and is alleged to have contact with Chinese intelligence.
Nvidia’s board is not considering bringing Huang back, CNBC reported on Monday. When he resigned, the board started a formal search for a permanent chief executive, according to Nvidia’s announcement. It will look at internal and external candidates. Colette Kress, the chief financial officer, is interim CEO. The board said on Friday it was choosing a search firm, CNBC reported.
Nvidia has hired the law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead its investigation, according to CNBC. The probe covers Huang’s conduct and whether it compromised national security or company secrets.
Huang has separately agreed to answer questions from three House committees on 1 December.

articles.title: Instagram is helping creators crack down on copycat videos
articles.text:
Instagram is beginning to roll out a “content protection” feature that lets creators see and review copies of their videos posted to the platform.
Instagram is helping creators crack down on copycat videos
Meta will let creators decide to hide copies of their videos flagged by a new ‘content protection’ feature.
“For eligible creators who enroll, content protection is a tool that automatically looks out for visual matches of your original videos, alerts you when we find a match across Instagram and Facebook, and lets you decide what happens next,” Meta says in a blog post. Meta launched a similar tool for Facebook last year to help users “safeguard” their Reels and “maintain control” over their creative work.
When an Instagram creator is notified of a matched video, they can see how many views the match has and decide if they want to track the video, hide it from everyone on Instagram and Facebook, add a credit link, or release their claim on the match.
After a creator enrolls, every “original video” they post on Instagram is protected, and creators can retroactively protect older videos manually. Creators can also put accounts on an allow list that lets them use their videos.
In addition, Instagram will start flagging AI-generated videos that “match the spoken words” in a creator’s original video but have visuals replaced with AI. Initially, Instagram will test this with a “small group of creators” in “the coming weeks.” The platform says it’s exploring ways to limit the reach of content and profiles that “use AI tools to post this type of content repeatedly.”

articles.title: Daydream's new AI agent acts as your personal stylist — and can shop for you, too | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Can an AI agent serve as your personal stylist? That’s what e-commerce veteran Julie Bornstein’s fashion startup, Daydream, aims to find out.
On Tuesday, the company launched “Daydream Agent,” an AI agent that is described as a personal stylist that can help you plan a look, virtually try on clothes, surface relevant pieces based on your taste, and more.
The idea, the company explains, is to put a personal stylist in everyone’s pocket. This application of AI could be promising, given that early adopters of consumer AI agents like Meta’s Muse have found that online shopping is a key use case.
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently noted that shopping was a top activity for Muse’s over 10 million users and that 25% of people who set up Muse now use it daily.
In Daydream’s case, the fashion startup has been focused on using AI to deliver personalized shopping results to its users. Its new AI agent builds on its earlier work with an AI chatbot that could help users find outfits and make suggestions, but not complete purchases.
Now the company says its Daydream Agent expands on that experience by remembering each shopper’s own personal style, fit preferences, and budget to refine its recommendations. Shoppers can also upload a photo to have the agent reuse that image to virtually try on any item they’ve saved. When they find something they like, the agent can complete a purchase through a one-click checkout process.
The agent can also handle other fashion-related tasks, like keeping an eye on when items go on sale or when brands have a new drop, or providing weekly updates or spotting new fashion trends.
Also, instead of leaving items in their cart, shoppers can save pieces they’re interested in to a persistent “clothing rack” so they can compare options and think about their purchases before deciding what to buy. Shoppers can also connect their own closet and their calendar to the agent, helping them to build outfits around what they already own and plan what to wear for upcoming events.
The tech works by pulling real-time pricing and availability information from its catalog of over 10,000 brands, then combines that with its fashion-focused artificial intelligence. It’s powered by a combination of OpenAI, Gemini, and Claude models, which it fine-tuned, along with its own trained models designed for particular use cases.
However, considering that fashion is more of an art than a science, the company says it’s keeping humans in the loop. To do so, this month it brought on its first stylist in residence, Francesca Salih, an international fashion stylist and the founder of StyleGrid. Salih provides the startup with styling content that helps shape how the agent pulls together outfits and offers advice. This advice is part of the company’s fashion knowledge database, which the agent experience relies on.
Bornstein, formerly Stitch Fix’s COO and the founder of The Yes (exited to Pinterest in 2022), started Daydream in 2023 as an AI search engine. The company, backed by $50 million in funding from Forerunner Ventures, Index Ventures, GV, and True Ventures, says more than 2 million shoppers have used Daydream to discover apparel and accessories since its June 2025 launch.

articles.title: Adam Mosseri thinks it will be 'pretty challenging' to design Instagram for the iPhone Duo - Engadget
articles.text:
Adam Mosseri thinks it will be 'pretty challenging' to design Instagram for the iPhone Duo
He says the app was made for tall vertical screens.
Adam Mosseri, the head of Instagram, says it's going to be "pretty challenging" to design the social media app "in a way that feels great" for the format of the iPhone Duo. Mosseri made the statement on Threads, where he also said that he came to the conclusion the more he looked at the details of the device.
A user responded, saying the best Instagram experience on the foldable is in portrait mode when the bigger screen is open, because the image takes up most of the display. Mosseri agreed that it was the best experience for Reels on Duo, but he added that Instagram is working to make the experience on other orientations better.
In another response, Mosseri explained that Instagram was designed for tall vertical screens. The Duo's form factor is far from typical, even when folded, as it's wider and shorter compared to most smartphones. As an example of an issue Instagram is trying to address, he said that it makes total sense for the navigation buttons on the right-hand side of the screen when it's closed as it's ergonomic that way. However, that's also where the Like, Comment and Share buttons are located in Reels. "Now we've got this double stack of buttons that doesn't feel great and that we need to reconsider," he said. "It's a lot of that kind of thing."
The Instagram app that was designed for the iPhone Duo has been out globally since October 23. However, it's gotten quite a bit of flak for its interface since then, with people specifically mentioning the double stack of buttons Mosseri was talking about. This could be Mosseri addressing the criticisms, or him trying to set people's expectations for when Instagram rolls out the next versions of its app for the device.

articles.title: Zelenskyy says Starshield speed curbs still in place over 'occupied territories' of Ukraine
articles.text:
American satellite service Starshield is still operating under speed limits in "occupied" parts of Ukraine, compromising the country's ability to defend itself against Russia, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in an X post on Tuesday.
"The speed limit on Starshield in the temporarily occupied territories remains in place. We are discussing this with the American side," Zelenskyy wrote.
He last week said Kyiv was investigating fresh restrictions on Starshield — developed by SpaceX for government use — over Ukraine, especially the front line and temporarily occupied territories. "There have already been strikes that got through because our interception systems cannot reach sufficient speeds and are unable to intercept in time."
Speed limits mean that Ukrainian drones flying around 100 miles per hour or faster lose Starshield internet connectivity, sometimes dropping out of the sky.
Kyiv has used interceptor drones to defend against Russian drone and missile strikes, as the country reportedly runs low on air defense missiles.
The ongoing Starshield restrictions Ukraine has reported come ahead of a trilateral meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen.
SpaceX CEO Elon Musk is expected to accompany Trump on the trip to China. The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
In late October, Ukrainian officials reported similar restrictions on the military-grade network, with both Trump and Musk denying that they had ordered the slowdown.
Musk had said that Starshield systems are "owned and controlled by the US government" and that any speed or usage limits are "decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS."
However, the Wall Street Journal reported Musk had ordered the slowdown, citing U.S. officials and people familiar with the matter.
Canadian Defense Minister David McGuinty said Wednesday ahead of the NATO Ukraine Defence Contact Group that he "was sure" that Prime Minister Mark Carney will raise the issue of Starshield restrictions with Trump.
— CNBC's Kevin Breuninger contributed to this report.

articles.title: China’s Xi calls for removing trade and investment barriers ahead of his meeting with Trump and Putin
articles.text:
Chinese President Xi Jinping looks on during a bilateral meeting with Vietnam's President To Lam on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China's Guangdong province on November 17, 2026.  
Maxim Shemetov | Afp | Getty Images
SHENZHEN, China — Chinese President Xi Jinping opened a key Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting on Wednesday with calls for removing trade and investment barriers.
The leader spoke as he was expected to host Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump this week alongside the APEC CEO and Economic Leaders Summit.
"China will not only cut tariffs and expand market access, but also go a step further," Xi said via an official English translation. He said China would "reform" rules and regulations to give foreign businesses "full manufacturing access."

articles.title: CCTV Script 18/11/26
articles.text:
– This is the script of CNBC's financial news report for China's CCTV on November 18, 2026.
The latest retail sales data came in slightly above market expectations, yet month over month growth moderated from 0.8% in September to 0.2%, signaling a slowdown in sales momentum. Looking at the consumption breakdown, retail gains were primarily driven by spending on essentials such as gasoline, while big ticket discretionary items including new vehicles and furniture struggled to move. Sales at gasoline stations rose 1.5% month over month in October, whereas motor vehicle and parts dealers saw sales decline 1.6%, and furniture and home furnishings dropped 2.3%.
Analysts point out that retail sales figures are not adjusted for inflation and reflect nominal spending rather than true changes in real consumption. Stripping out price increases, October retail sales may have actually registered negative growth. Data released last week showed that the US Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% month over month in October, exceeding market forecasts.
Alongside decelerating retail sales growth, underlying support for household consumption appears fragile. Data previously published by the US Bureau of Economic Analysis showed that after adjusting for inflation and personal taxes, real disposable personal income fell 0.3% month over month in September, marking the first decline since April of this year. Furthermore, the recent tech led equity selloff could erode the wealth effect generated by stock market gains, prompting high income households to tighten spending. Meanwhile, low and middle income households are increasingly relying on credit and drawing down savings to sustain consumption. Data indicates that the US personal saving rate dropped to 3.8% in September, nearing a four year low, while average balances on active credit card accounts are climbing at an annualized pace of over 9%, the fastest rate since the pandemic.
CLAUDIA SAHM
Chief Economist, Founder
Sahm Consulting
"And one of the things that's missing from earlier, like in the pandemic in 21 and 22, when there was more inflation, the labor market was really strong, and you saw a lot of workers, especially low wage workers, switching jobs to get higher wages, like that, is not an option right now. The labor market's not strong for that."
IAN SHEPHERDSON
Founder, Chairman, Editor in Chief
Pantheon Macroeconomics
"The bigger risk for U.S. economic growth over the course of the next year is that the consumer slows down. If the stock market is going to wobble or even just to flatline, that strength in consumer spending will begin to fade away."
Rising prices are squeezing household budgets, and if inflation proves sticky, the Federal Reserve will be forced to continue tightening monetary policy. St. Louis Fed President Musalem warned on Tuesday that the United States may need multiple interest rate hikes before spring 2027 to restore price stability in a timely manner. Currently, several institutions including Goldman Sachs project that the Fed could deliver a cumulative three rate hikes by March of next year, lifting the federal funds target range to between 4.5% and 4.75% from the current 3.75% to 4%. Higher borrowing costs could in turn further restrain household spending, leaving the US economy facing the dual headwinds of slowing consumption and monetary tightening toward year end.

articles.title: Analysts are cautiously optimistic on Nvidia after earnings call
articles.text: Analysts were hopeful about Nvidia' s near-term performance prospects following the company's highly anticipated third-quarter earnings call Tuesday amid the ongoing leadership crisis at the critical U.S. chipmaker. Uncertainties are swirling around Nvidia in light of former CEO Jensen Huang's involvement with a woman who intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy, according to The New York Times . The Wall Street Journal also reported Tuesday, citing people familiar, that the Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating the company. However, analysts saw some points of clarity through the fog. Nvidia increased its fiscal year 2028 revenue growth outlook to 75% from 70%, which impressed analysts in light of all the difficulties now facing the company. NVDA 3M mountain Nvidia over the past three months "That's by far the most important thing that happened," Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson said. Certainty around leadership Nvidia's chairman Harvey Jones gave a definitive negative answer to the question of whether Huang would be able to return to his role at the company, which Wall Street analysts appreciated. "Certainly one thing stood out when chair of the board Harvey Jones said the board accepted Jensen's resignation unanimously and … he will not be inviting him back," James Kelleher, director of research at Argus told CNBC. Cody Acree at StoneX said the decision on Huang made sense and was the right thing to do despite the ramifications for Nvidia's business. "There has to be a line in the sand that the board has to consider, and I think they were right to do so. Nvidia is not going to be the same company without Jensen, but there are some things that can't be ignored," he said. China sales Up to 10% of Nvidia's sales may come directly or indirectly from China , according to an analysis from New Street Research. On Tuesday's call, interim-CEO Colette Kress said that third-quarter sales of its licensed Hopper chips and products into China amounted to $2.4 billion and that the company was going to stop selling these into China. This came as "a bit of a surprise" to Acree, though the plan to change course did not. "The surprise is that they were able to sell anything at all – so a nice, near-term contribution, but the better part of valor is to assume nothing to China, and that's what they baked into their expectation," he said, referring to the company's revenue forecast. What's next for financing deals Regarding Nvidia's numerous financing and vendor arrangements, Kress said on the call that Nvidia would be "rigorously evaluating" future deals and stressed the contingency of past guarantees and backstops the company has provided. However, Kress also said the company will be advancing with some future deals as part of its overall capital allocation structure, which includes returning capital to shareholders. "There will be a portion that we will do, but again, [there will be] a lot of work to understand if those are the right types of investments that we need to make," she said. Luria at D.A. Davidson thought the option to reconsider deals was a positive indication of flexibility. "They're saying, we made these commitments, we're moving forward, this is how much they are. But if we need to move away from them, we can do that, as well. I thought that was a positive update," he said. "It's somewhat of a relief to all these companies getting capital from Nvidia, but I would temper their enthusiasm with the fact that they left room to pull back from all these programs," Luria added. The so-called neoclouds that get financing and backstopping from Nvidia responded positively to the call, with CoreWeave up 9%, Iren up 10% and Nebius up 11% in after-hours trading on Tuesday evening.

articles.title: LeBron James sues startup over viral AI ad allegedly exploiting his likeness
articles.text:
NBA superstar LeBron James sued artificial intelligence-powered sports betting startup Bron and its two founders, accusing them of using his name, likeness and AI-generated voice without permission to promote their app.
In a lawsuit filed Tuesday in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, James accused PlayVision, which operates the Bron app, and co-founders Anish Gupta and Marc Zoghby of deliberately exploiting his "Bron" nickname to mislead consumers into believing he endorsed or was affiliated with the app.
The complaint alleges that the startup released an AI-generated advertisement earlier this month depicting James in a basketball locker room, wearing a jersey bearing his nickname and the iconic number 23, along with his tattoos and a simulated version of his voice.
The video showed the AI-generated figure scrolling through NBA betting options on the app.
James alleged that the defendants deliberately sought to provoke controversy to generate publicity for their app, with the advertisement attracting about one million views on X within a day.
The lawsuit claims the founders calculated that the publicity would outweigh any potential legal consequences, effectively treating the alleged violation of James' rights as a marketing expense.
It argues that James' endorsements are "uniquely valuable," adding, "That is why defendants decided to steal it for themselves."
The NBA star's lawyers sent a cease-and-desist letter on Nov. 5, after which the startup removed the ad from its X and Instagram accounts and said it was working to change the app's name, according to the complaint.
However, the ad remained available through third-party reposts, and the company had not changed the app's name as of the lawsuit's filing.
James is seeking damages and a court order preventing the defendants from using his name, image, likeness, and voice, as well as the Bron name.
Bron, operated by PlayVision, is described in Apple's App Store as a "sports analytics and betting research app with live odds comparisons, data-backed picks, player and team trends, a multi-leg Slip and bet tracking." The listing says it does not accept wagers.
PlayVision is headquartered in California and participated in Y Combinator's fall 2025 batch.
— CNBC's Dan Mangan contributed to this story.

articles.title: OpenAI bugging case defendant Alfozan set for trial in January
articles.text:
A federal judge on Tuesday set Jan. 20 for the start of the trial for Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan, who is accused of planting a recording device in an OpenAI conference room when he worked for the artificial intelligence company as an engineering lead.
If the trial starts on that date in U.S. District Court in San Francisco, it would be after an unusually short lag since Alfozan's arrest in October. Federal criminal cases, as a rule, do not go to trial so quickly.
But Alfozan's attorney, David Rizk, sought the speedy trial after complaining at a court hearing that prosecutors have been slow in turning over evidence in the case.
Rizk also said prosecutors have not given him any evidence that Alfozan engaged in espionage, after they argued successfully last month that he should be detained without bail, and after saying his alleged bugging "could pose a danger to the national security of the United States."
Among other things, prosecutors had noted that Alfozan is a venture partner at Saudi venture firm Raed Ventures alongside a member of the Saudi royal family, Prince Khalid bin Bader Al Saud.
Alfozan, who has pleaded not guilty in the case, is charged with one count of intercepting oral communications. He faces a maximum of five years in prison if he is convicted.
Prosecutors have said Alfozan was arrested after staff at OpenAI found a recording device wrapped in toilet paper and installed in the back of a television in the conference room at its San Francisco headquarters in September. A surveillance camera captured Alfozan looking at the gadget in the room.
Assistant U.S. Attorney Nick Parker told Judge Vince Chhabria on Tuesday that government investigators have been locked out of Alfozan's phone, but they have also collected one other phone, a tablet, and two laptops.
Prosecutors also obtained 160 hours of recordings from meetings in a conference room.
The recording device itself is encrypted, but if data was backed up to another device, investigators would have been able to obtain it, Parker said.
Chhabria told prosecutors that they must turn over all reports the FBI has created to Alfozan's attorney by Nov. 24, and that they must also move quickly to give the defense other evidence for use at trial.
"We need to make sure that you get whatever discovery you're entitled to promptly," Chhabria told Rizk.
OpenAI, which fired Alfozan after his arrest, has said it lacked proof of him taking source code or customer data.
Chhabria also told Parker he wants to see, within seven days, any evidence that might exist showing Alfozan carrying out economic espionage, stealing trade secrets or acting as an unregistered foreign agent.
Parker said he was not aware of any such evidence at this time.
"At this point, I'm not suggesting the defendant stole anything," Parker said.
The prosecutor told the judge that his team had a "serious concern" about Rizk's plans to review evidence turned over to the defense with an AI tool that competes with OpenAI. Parker noted that among the seized evidence is a laptop that might have proprietary OpenAI data.
Chhabria replied, "I'm a lot less concerned about that than you are."
The judge ordered Parker to submit a motion by Friday explaining why the defense's use of a competing AI to analyze evidence might be a problem.
Rizk told CNBC he intends to use Anthropic's Claude. Anthropic, which aims to go public on Nasdaq this week, was founded by OpenAI employees.
— CNBC's Dan Mangan contributed to this report.

articles.title: Nvidia takes positive step forward with stronger sales outlook. Here’s our thoughts on the stock
articles.text: Nvidia shares jumped in extended trading Tuesday after the AI chipmaker reported strong quarterly results. In a sign of continued momentum in the business, interim CEO Colette Kress also raised the company's revenue growth outlook for its next fiscal year. Revenue in the company's fiscal 2027 third quarter increased 103% to $115.84 billion, outpacing the $109.11 billion consensus, according to estimates compiled by data provider LSEG. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) increased 111% to $2.68, also exceeding the LSEG consensus estimate of $2.48. Adjusted gross margin of 74.9% improved by 140 basis points year over year and exceeded the FactSet consensus estimate of 74.27%. Shares were up about 5% in after-hours trading in response to the big beat and raise. Even with this much-needed after-hours rally, Nvidia shares are still down about $10 since former CEO Jensen Huang's resignation last Thursday. NVDA YTD mountain Nvidia's year-to-date stock performance. Bottom line Nvidia's results show that the company still has the best performing AI chips around, with demand continuing to exceed supply. The company is one quarter into shipments of its next-generation Vera Rubin compute racks, and its nearly $20 billion in revenue for the quarter made it the fastest product ramp in company history. But what the market is struggling to figure out is what Nvidia looks like in a post-Huang world. The chair of Nvidia's board, Harvey Jones, made it clear at the top of Tuesday's earnings call that there are no plans to bring Huang back as CEO. "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," Jones said. Earlier in the day, Huang said in a statement that would be open to returning as CEO if the board determined it was "in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America." The leadership shake-up did not stop Kress from increasing Nvidia's revenue outlook for fiscal year 2028, which begins in February. On the call, Kress said the company expects revenues to grow 75% year over year, up from its prior outlook of 70%. That initial 70% target for FY28 was unexpectedly issued back in August and was considered a very bullish update. Keep in mind: this updated growth figure is off a much higher base for fiscal year 2027, given the better-than-expected numbers Nvidia reported Tuesday night. Doing math on what 75% growth looks like, Nvidia now sees fiscal year 2028 revenue of about $741.44 billion, which is roughly 7% above the FactSet consensus of $692.35 billion. That also means the stock right now is even cheaper than its price-to-earnings multiple of 10 on fiscal 2028 estimated earnings. Kress issuing an even stronger 2028 guide was a true upside surprise — and not just because the numbers were better than expected. It was meaningful because many believed Nvidia would refrain from giving any type of guide and specifically retract Huang's 70% forecast given the uncertainty at the company. The fact that Kress provided guidance signals confidence in Nvidia's ability to continue performing at the highest level without its founder at the helm. As for the rest of the quarter and call, Kress did not offer a change in the way Nvidia supports supply chain with financing. However, when it comes to financing customers, we heard a more disciplined tone from Kress during her exclusive interview with Jim on "Mad Money." This was one of the many questions we had into earnings. Nvidia put its monster buyback program to work in the third quarter, repurchasing $22 billion worth of stock in the quarter. When you add in dividend payments, Nvidia's total capital returns in the three months ended in October totaled $28.1 billion. Recall, in late September, Nvidia announced a $150 billion increase to its share repurchase authorization, bringing its total buyback program to $235 billion — the largest in history. The company ended the third quarter with $227.3 billion remaining on its authorization, and we would expect them to be extremely active in the market buying stock down here. "All things considered, we walk away from the quarter and Jim's interview with Kress feeling encouraged about the demand for Nvidia's chips. Based on that alone, this is certainly an attractive job for someone within the tech industry. At the same time, we cannot ignore there are still many questions surrounding the company. Accordingly, we are lowering our price target to $200 from $280. Although earnings per share estimates for fiscal 2028 will increase following tonight's strong report, we expect the stock's price-to-earnings multiple to remain constrained due to all that uncertainty. We're also keeping our 2/"not rated" view on the stock for now. While a departure from our normal convention, we unpacked what that means in Monday's Homestretch. Quarterly commentary Data Center segment revenue for the quarter was $107.61 billion, well ahead of estimates of $101.87 billion. That was up 110% year over year and nearly 21% sequentially. There are two sub-segments within Data Center: Hyperscale sales — consisting of public clouds and the world's largest consumer internet companies like Amazon , Microsoft , Meta Platforms , and Alphabet — increased 71% year over year to $60.13 billion. This was much better than expected. Hyperscale cloud revenue growth accelerated for the sixth consecutive quarter, this time led by the ramp of Vera Rubin generation chips and continued strength in the Glace Blackwell family. Kress pointed out that cloud industry backlog is now at $2.5 trillion, up from $2 trillion last quarter. This gives a multiyear line of sight into demand for Nvidia chips, but it's fair to wonder if that number will come down in the future if politics make it tougher for data centers to get built in the next few years. AI Clouds, Industrial, & Enterprise (ACIE) sales are from purpose-built AI data centers and AI factories across other industries and countries. Revenue here was $47.47 billion, which missed analyst forecasts of about $48.99 billion. Sales to these customers were up 195% year over year and 18% sequentially. Driving the strong growth were shipments of Vera Rubin systems to leading neocloud customers such as CoreWeave and Nebius , along with frontier AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic beginning to build their own data centers. Sales in the Edge Computing segment include many of Nvidia's legacy parts — think devices for agentic and physical AI, including personal computers (PCs), game consoles, workstations, robotics, automotive, and the so-called AI radio access network . Segment revenue totaled $8.2 billion, up 42% year over year and above expectations by $763 million. Similar to the dynamic from the previous quarters, Blackwell workstation demand remains strong. Financial commitments In the earnings release, Nvidia provided an update on the now $518 billion in financial commitments that it has made through agreements, partnerships, and investments. Future commitments are up from $366 billion last quarter. The figure is made up of: $390 billion of commitments to supply and capacity. This is up from $279 billion last quarter, primarily due to the multiyear procurement of memory supply. $28 billion of cloud service agreements and $74 billion of data center leases not commenced. This combined $102 billion of commitments is up from $54 billion last quarter. $20 billion in equity investments And $6 billion of capital expenditures. Nvidia spent some time detailing the $32 billion of commitments it has with neoclouds. Nvidia makes these deals because it earns revenue from the upfront sale of its infrastructure and participates in the upside in rental revenue above a minimum commitment. Nvidia clarified these arrangements in the press release and earnings call, noting that its commitments "take effect only if the neoclouds secure financing to purchase the data center infrastructure products and the related compute capacity is deployed, made operational, and accepted by us." The guarantee no longer exists if a project is delayed, or if there is a challenge building the data center. "Neoclouds remain an increasingly important part of the global AI infrastructure ecosystem, providing additional customers with access to Nvidia compute and expanding the reach of our platform," Kress said on the call. "We have supported the development of this ecosystem, and we will continue to be disciplined and selective in our support." Guidance Looking ahead to Nvidia's current fiscal 2027 fourth quarter, management's outlook was strong on the top line and the forecast for gross margins bracketed expectations. The company expects revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, ahead of the $125.25 billion LSEG consensus estimate. This guide calls for revenue growth of about 90.8% in the fourth quarter. Consistent with prior quarters, guidance continues to reflect zero data center compute revenue from China. Don't expect that to happen any time soon. Adjusted gross margins are expected to be between 71.0% and 72.0%, which brackets the consensus estimate of 71.7%, according to FactSet. Elevated memory prices have taken a chunk out of gross margins, but the fourth quarter is expected to be a near term bottom. Nvidia expects gross margins to improve to the 72% to 73% range in fiscal year 2028. (Jim Cramer's Charitable Trust is long NVDA. See here for a full list of the stocks.) articles.title: Three things to watch as Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China
articles.text:
SHENZHEN, China — Leaders of the U.S., China, Russia and other major Asia-Pacific economies face a series of critical issues from wars to tech security as they gather for an annual summit this week.
Since the last APEC leaders' meeting, China's tensions with Japan have escalated. Barely stabilized U.S.-China relations face new tests in the wake of Washington's scrutiny of Nvidia's China chip sales. And the Iran war, now in its ninth month, is still pressuring global energy prices, while the Russia-Ukraine war has dragged on.
But expectations are low for any breakthroughs.
Meanwhile for Beijing, host to this year's series of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings, the multilateral gathering is yet another venue to build its global influence. Chinese President Xi Jinping met Tuesday with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and the President of Vietnam To Lam. Vietnam is hosting next year's APEC meetings.
Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Shenzhen early Wednesday morning, where he was greeted by Chinese Politburo Standing Committee Member Cai Qi, according to Chinese state media. U.S. President Donald Trump is in the Philippines for the ASEAN Summit before heading to Shenzhen.
Here's what's at stake this week:
1. U.S.-China talks
Trump and Xi are expected to meet alongside the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting Wednesday and Thursday. Their summit around the gathering last year in South Korea ushered in a one-year trade truce of lower tariffs and some rare earths flows, which was extended by two months, to January 2027.
In this week's summit, Trump does not plan to raise the issue of Nvidia and allegations that its former CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a Chinese spy, U.S. officials said. They said the talks would focus on implementing the trade agreement.
The U.S. and China in September said they would lower tariffs on $30 billion worth of goods from the other country, without specifying an effective date. China said this month that it would only increase purchases of U.S. agricultural products if those tariffs were lowered.
However, Washington is already moving to tighten restrictions on loopholes that had given Chinese companies access to American artificial intelligence technology. So far, China's response has been to threaten countermeasures.
"If there is room for genuine U.S.-China cooperation this week, it's on managing risk rather than sharing advantage," said Reema Bhattacharya, head of Asia research at risk intelligence company Verisk Maplecroft. That could include cooperation on an artificial intelligence security hotline.
"Across Asia, governments under mounting pressure to pick a side will be watching Shenzhen for signs of how much room they still have to maneuver," Bhattacharya said. "Most have little appetite for a region split into two technology camps."
2. Geopolitical posturing
On Thursday, Xi is set to meet with Trump and Putin, according to Beijing's official confirmation of the event, billed as the "China-Russia-U.S. Summit."
It's the first-ever gathering of the three leaders, albeit with low expectations that there will be sufficient time for thorough dialogue. But the event creates the opportunity for a globally influential photo-op similar to the one that Xi, Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi had on the sidelines of a China-hosted Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in September 2025.
Also closely watched will be any interaction with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. Last November, her comments drew Beijing's ire after indicating Tokyo would support Taiwan if the island were seriously threatened by Beijing's military.
Takaichi is expected to join the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in her first trip to China since becoming prime minister. She had met Xi on the sidelines of the APEC event last year in South Korea.
Attendees from other APEC economies are hoping for more signs of cooperation.
Anindya Bakrie, CEO of Indonesian conglomerate Bakrie & Brothers, told CNBC that when Trump and Xi meet, the narrative is hopefully one of peace and stability.
3. Tech
Tech issues are likely to be in heavy focus. Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk is set to join Trump on the Shenzhen trip. Other American executives, such as Visa CEO Ryan McInerney, joined a two-day APEC CEO Summit that kicked off Tuesday.
The APEC host city, Shenzhen, has been dubbed one of China's "Silicon Valleys" and is home to Huawei and BYD. The summit organizers are also using the event to showcase local robotics startups.
A slew of tech company earnings is coming out at the same time as the APEC meeting, keeping the corporate side in the spotlight as well.
Nvidia released quarterly results Wednesday morning Beijing time, following a tumultuous two weeks of scrutiny that forced the chipmaker's founder Jensen Huang to resign. The company boosted its outlook and shares rose in extended trading.
Shenzhen-based gaming and social media giant Tencent is set to report its quarterly earnings Wednesday evening. The company has previously noted constraints from its limited computing power.
U.S.-based AI giant Anthropic is pricing its highly anticipated initial public offering this week, and expected to list on the Nasdaq Thursday Nov. 19. Its CEO Dario Amodei has urged a slowdown in AI development and warned of the risk if China does not follow suit.
—CNBC's Penny Chen and Anniek Bao contributed to this report.

articles.title: Nvidia's Colette Kress tells Cramer: Employees and customers are not going anywhere
articles.text:
Nvidia's customers and employees remain committed to the company despite last week's abrupt departure of longtime leader Jensen Huang. That's the message interim CEO Colette Kress conveyed exclusively to CNBC's Jim Cramer shortly after the AI chip giant delivered a quarterly beat and strong guidance.
"[Hyperscalers] are the ones that are right now feverishly looking for more focus in terms of the compute that we have available," Kress said on "Mad Money." "This concept that anything is changing in terms of any of our types of customers — that is just not true. They are all continuing to be with us, and we have a very deep breath of different customers."
Kress' comments came after Nvidia reported better-than-expected quarterly earnings and revenue and bumped up its fiscal 2028 revenue growth estimate to 75% from the previous 70%. It was the first earnings report since Huang's resignation as CEO amid a widening affair scandal. Shares rose nearly 4% in after-hours trading as the results helped ease concerns about the chipmaker's outlook following the leadership shake-up.
Some on Wall Street have wondered whether Huang's departure would prompt certain Nvidia customers to lean harder into their in-house designed chips and/or competitors such as Advanced Micro Devices.
During the "Mad Money" interview Tuesday evening, Kress emphasized that major customers have continued expressing interest in the company's products. "I have seen already with many of these [customers] contacting me and saying, 'Great to see everything intact. Great to see that there's more supply. I need more demand.'"
Customer demand, however, wasn't the only issue facing Nvidia. Huang's departure has also raised questions about whether the chipmaker can retain the engineers and other employees who helped build its dominance in artificial intelligence. The co-founder was widely viewed as the driving force behind Nvidia's technology and corporate culture.
Kress dismissed concerns about a potential employee exodus, stressing to Cramer that the workforce's longstanding commitment to the company is intact, and so is support from the leadership team. "The company has been built under the perspective that the employees look at Nvidia as their life work, and many of them have been here for many decades, working with us both from a technology standpoint or a business and operations perspective," she said.
"We have high confidence that our employees are definitely still working, still working with us, and enjoy ... the work here at Nvidia," Kress told Cramer.

articles.title: Japan exports in October surge 20.5%, beating estimates on robust chip shipments
articles.text:
Japan's exports in October surged 20.5% from a year earlier, snapping a two-month slowdown in shipments, official data released Wednesday showed.
Exports growth beat expectations of economists polled by Reuters that had pegged it at 20%, and it was sharply higher compared to a revised 16.5% in September.
Shipments of semiconductor equipment that have been propping up Tokyo's exports jumped 49.7% by value. Exports of motor vehicles climbed 19.9% year on year.
In terms of destinations, shipments to China rose 13.3%, while they climbed 23.9% to the U.S.
Exports have been the main driver of Japan's growth, although a surge in the value of imports of petroleum due to the Iran war has offset some the impact of the exports surge on its economy.
Import growth in Japan for October came in at 21.6%, sharply missing analysts' estimates of 25.8%, with petroleum imports climbing 60.5% by value, even as volumes slipped 0.7%.
Analysts previously told CNBC that the surge in value was because Japan was attempting to switch sources to more expensive American oil as shipments from the Middle East stalled.
Imports of petroleum from the U.S. jumped more than 1,100% year on year by value and 738% by volume. In contrast, shipments from the Middle East dipped 16.5% by volume, while higher prices pushed up import value by 37.7%.
The country posted a surprise contraction in its third quarter GDP, which shrank 0.1% on an annualized basis.
Following the data, Japan's Nikkei 225 was up 0.91%, while the yen traded at 159.50 to the dollar.

articles.title: A sluggish housing market has held back Home Depot. Here's Cramer's advice on the stock now
articles.text:
Mad Money
A sluggish housing market has held back Home Depot. Here's Cramer's advice on the stock now
Key Points
- Jim Cramer said Home Depot's latest earnings report strengthened his confidence in the retailer's long-term prospects.
- He pointed to improving demand and market-share gains as reasons to buy the dip, arguing that Home Depot is well-positioned to benefit from an eventual housing recovery.
CNBC's Jim Cramer said that Home Depot's third-quarter earnings report strengthened his confidence in the retailer's long-term prospects, rendering the stock's pullback Tuesday a buying opportunity. "I told CNBC Investing Club members today that, if we weren't restricted in the name, I would be buying today's dip and adding more Home Depot shares for my Charitable Trust," the " Mad Money " host said. "This was a good quarter, and the negative response just seems to be based on a myopic view of what the company was implying about the current quarter with its updated guidance." Shares of the home improvement retailer fell 2% despite reporting better-than-expected quarterly earnings and revenue. Same-store sales climbed 2.2%, marking the retailer's strongest comps performance in four years. The sell-off appeared driven by updated full-year guidance that implied slightly weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter results. But Cramer cautioned against reading too much into the forecast, noting Home Depot's history of conservative guidance, particularly as it prepares for a leadership transition. The company announced Tuesday that veteran CFO Richard McPhail will succeed Ted Decker as CEO next week. Decker, who went on temporary medical leave in August, will continue to serve as chair of the board. Home Depot shares have struggled to gain traction in recent years, as elevated interest rates weighed on housing activity and home improvement spending. Higher mortgage rates have discouraged homeowners from moving, reducing demand for the renovation projects that often accompany home sales. Shares have shown signs of life since reaching a 52-week low on Oct. 1, rallying roughly 20%, as bond yields retreated and investors rotated into consumer stocks. Still, the stock remains down 1% for the year. But Cramer argued that Home Depot's latest results offer reasons to own the stock while waiting for a decline in interest rates to spark a meaningful inflection for the business. "I heard enough from management to stay invested now, and I feel even better about the long-term prospects of Home Depot after today's report," he said. On the earnings call, incoming CEO McPhail highlighted strength in the repair and remodeling businesses, while 13 of Home Depot's 16 product categories posted positive comparable sales and online sales continued growing at a double-digit pace. Cramer said those encouraging demand trends, along with market-share gains among professional contractors, suggest Home Depot is strengthening its business even before the housing market recovers. "For those with a long-term view, the important part is that the company is taking share," he said. "Whenever the broader housing market does return, Home Depot is positioned to be one of the companies that stands to benefit the most." articles.title: Jim Cramer’s key takeaway from Nvidia’s first earnings since Huang’s resignation
articles.text:
Key Points
- Jim Cramer said Nvidia's blockbuster earnings strengthened his confidence in the chipmaker's future under new leadership.
- He said a new CEO could bring greater financial discipline by scaling back investments across the AI ecosystem and redirecting more cash toward share buybacks.
CNBC's Jim Cramer said Tuesday that Nvidia's blockbuster earnings reinforced his confidence in the chipmaker's business and its future under new leadership. "We need to focus on the fundamentals and on those, boy, oh boy, is this stock ever cheap," the " Mad Money " host said. "You know what that does? It gives me hope that there'll be plenty of really great candidates to run this company and do it in a responsible way, and figure out a way to stop throwing money at anything that moves in the data center while spending more money buying its very cheap stock back, as [interim CEO] Colette Kress knows all too well." Nvidia beat earnings and revenue expectations Tuesday and issued strong guidance in its first quarterly report since Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation as CEO last week, amid a widening affair scandal. Revenue more than doubled from a year earlier, exceeding estimates by nearly $7 billion, while earnings topped expectations by 20 cents per share. Shares of Nvidia initially fell in extended trading Tuesday after board Chairman Harvey Jones said on the earnings call that the company wasn't interested in bringing Huang back as CEO. But the stock later rebounded, rising 4% after Kress raised Nvidia's revenue outlook for next fiscal year and highlighted robust customer demand. "To no one's surprise, [the results] were phenomenal – the numbers were never the issue here," Cramer said. Kress came on "Mad Money" shortly after the earnings call ended and exclusively talked to Cramer about the path forward after Huang. She stressed that demand for Nvidia's AI chips is only increasing, with hyperscalers "feverishly looking" for supply. She said that not only are customers and partners sticking with Nvidia, but so are the employees. She also reiterated to Cramer that the board has said it won't reinstate Huang as CEO, adding that leadership at the company is focusing on ways to grow the business, as well as working with employees and shareholders. The strong earnings performance and encouraging words from Kress are bolstering Cramer's belief that Nvidia can thrive without Huang , potentially with a new CEO who takes a more disciplined approach to spending. Cramer has in recent days recommended that investors sitting on big gains in Nvidia take some off the table, as Huang's departure represented a major shift in the company's narrative. But he has also emphasized that Nvidia is bigger than any one person and argued that the talent within the company remains a valuable asset going forward. Under Huang, Nvidia amassed a broad portfolio of investments across the AI ecosystem and made other financial commitments to customers, including a $105 billion backstop for a massive data center project planned for OpenAI. Cramer said scaling back those investments and redirecting more cash toward repurchasing Nvidia's shares could help the chipmaker move beyond its leadership shake-up and restore investor confidence. articles.title: JPMorgan is working on AI agent transactions that don’t involve humans
articles.text:
Artificial intelligence agents have already proven to be helpful, or cause a lot of trouble, or both. One area seen as high-potential is in payments, where — if they're able to be trusted — the agents could deal with all sorts of money matters on behalf of people.
That's why JPMorgan Chase and South Korea's Hyundai Card are testing how AI agents can handle financial transactions without direct human intervention, including whether they can eventually negotiate and make payments with one another.
The companies have completed an initial proof-of-concept involving a simulated foreign exchange transaction and are targeting the first half of 2027 for a more complex phase involving multiple AI agents.
What happens when agents are negotiating, agreeing directly with each other and then making payments? What does that actually look like?Wee Kee TohGlobal Head, Kinexys Insights
Wee Kee Toh, global head of Kinexys Insights at Kinexys by JP Morgan, told CNBC that the next step is to test what happens when autonomous agents move beyond execution and begin interacting with each other in an ecosystem.
"That, I would say, is really the biggest part of what we want to get as an expansion of the phase one scope," he added.
The initial trial involved a Hyundai Card AI agent requesting a foreign exchange transaction to maintain euro liquidity in its Kinexys blockchain deposit account. JPMorgan said it was the first private blockchain-based autonomous bank-agent-to-client-agent test for corporate treasury management.
Beyond the pilot
While the initial trial has been completed, JPMorgan has yet to set a timeline for commercializing the technology.
Toh said building the technology itself was relatively straightforward, but establishing appropriate governance and internal controls proved more difficult.
"Technology-wise, it's really not the biggest hurdle," he said, pointing instead to questions around accountability and the risks of allowing AI agents to execute financial transactions without direct human oversight.
To address those concerns, Kinexys developed a framework that restricts AI agents to predefined transaction parameters, automatically rejecting requests that fall outside authorized limits.
"You are going to draw a box around the agent. The agent will never be able to do anything out of the box," Toh said.
For example, an AI agent authorized to transact up to $5 million would be blocked from executing transactions above that threshold, he said.
The companies are also exploring whether to extend their collaboration to other businesses within Hyundai Motor Group, whose broader operations were one reason JPMorgan selected Hyundai Card as a partner, Toh said. No specific projects have been announced.
Hyundai Motor Group holds a combined 78.04% stake in Hyundai Card through Hyundai Motor, Kia and Hyundai Commercial, according to the card issuer's website.
Hyundai Card has previously experimented with blockchain-based cross-border payments. In July, the company said it completed a proof-of-concept involving a $20,000 transfer using the USDT stablecoin between Hyundai Motor's U.S. and Mexican subsidiaries, with the transfer and verification process taking an average of seven minutes.
Kinexys has also been expanding its blockchain-based payments business. The JPMorgan unit said in August that it had processed more than $4 trillion in transactions since inception, averaging about $7 billion a day.
Separately, JPMorgan launched a proof-of-concept for its dollar-denominated deposit token, JPMD, in June 2025, before making it available to institutional clients that November.
